<!-- source: https://docs.cartesi.io/cartesi-rollups/2.0/api-reference/contracts/consensus/overview/ -->

---
id: overview
title: Overview
resources:
  - url: https://github.com/cartesi/rollups-contracts/tree/v3.0.0-alpha.10/src/consensus
    title: Consensus Smart Contracts
---

The consensus mechanism in Cartesi Rollups is responsible for validating, staging and accepting claims submitted by validators. These contracts ensure the integrity of the rollup by deciding which outputs Merkle roots are valid, so that the [`Application`](../application.md) contract can validate and execute outputs.

## Consensus Contracts

The framework supports different consensus mechanisms:

- **[Authority](./authority/authority.md)**: Single-owner consensus controlled by one address
- **[Quorum](./quorum/quorum.md)**: Multi-validator consensus requiring majority approval

Both are deployed through factories ([`AuthorityFactory`](./authority/authority-factory.md), [`QuorumFactory`](./quorum/quorum-factory.md)) that take the epoch length and the claim staging period.

:::note PRT applications
Applications that use PRT (fraud proofs with permissionless dispute tournaments) use the [`DaveConsensus`](https://github.com/cartesi/dave/tree/v3.0.0-alpha.6/cartesi-rollups/contracts/src/DaveConsensus.sol) contract from the [cartesi/dave](https://github.com/cartesi/dave/tree/v3.0.0-alpha.6) repository. `DaveConsensus` implements [`IOutputsMerkleRootValidator`](./ioutputs-merkle-root-validator.md), but not `IConsensus`: it has no `submitClaim()` or `acceptClaim()`, and its epochs are settled through tournaments. The `IConsensus` lifecycle below does not apply to it.
:::

## Core Interfaces

- **[IConsensus](./iconsensus.md)**: Main interface defining the consensus contract behavior
- **[IOutputsMerkleRootValidator](./ioutputs-merkle-root-validator.md)**: Interface the `Application` contract uses to validate outputs, prove the accounts drive and decide refunds
- **[AbstractConsensus](./abstract-consensus.md)**: Abstract implementation providing common consensus functionality

## Consensus Mechanism

A claim consists of:

- Application Contract Address: The address of the application being validated
- Last Processed Block Number: The last block of the epoch the claim covers
- Machine Merkle Root: The root hash of the post-epoch machine state

When submitting a claim, the validator also sends a machine validity proof. From it, the consensus checks that the post-epoch machine is in a valid state and proves the **outputs Merkle root** (the root of the Merkle tree of all outputs produced by the application), which is stored in the machine memory.

The consensus contract validates that:
- The block number is at the end of an epoch (modulo epoch length equals epoch length - 1)
- The block number is in the past (not future)
- No duplicate claim has been submitted for the same application and epoch (by the same validator, in the case of a quorum)
- The application is deployed and not foreclosed

### Claim lifecycle

1. **Submit.** A validator calls `submitClaim(appContract, lastProcessedBlockNumber, machineMerkleRoot, proof)`. The consensus emits `ClaimSubmitted`.
2. **Stage.** When the claim meets the staging criteria of the consensus model, it is staged and the consensus emits `ClaimStaged`. In an `Authority`, a claim submitted by the owner is staged immediately. In a `Quorum`, a claim is staged when a majority of the validators (`1 + N/2`) submit the same machine Merkle root for the epoch.
3. **Wait.** The claim stays staged for at least `getClaimStagingPeriod()` blocks. During this period, the application guardian can foreclose the application, which prevents the claim from being accepted.
4. **Accept.** After the staging period, **anyone** can call `acceptClaim(appContract, lastProcessedBlockNumber, machineMerkleRoot)`. The consensus emits `ClaimAccepted`, and the claim's outputs Merkle root becomes valid. Only then can outputs of that epoch be validated and executed in the application contract.

A staged claim is not accepted automatically: someone must call `acceptClaim()` once the staging period is over. The Cartesi Rollups Node sends this transaction for the applications it validates. Calls made before the end of the staging period revert with `ClaimStagingPeriodNotOverYet`.

:::caution Choosing the claim staging period
The claim staging period is the window the guardian has to react to a bad claim. With a staging period of 0, a staged claim can be accepted in the same block in which it was staged, so the guardian has no window. Set it to a number of blocks larger than the time the guardian needs to notice a bad claim and foreclose the application.
:::

Use `getClaim()` to read the status of a claim (`UNSTAGED`, `STAGED` or `ACCEPTED`), and `getNumberOfSubmittedClaims()`, `getNumberOfStagedClaims()` and `getNumberOfAcceptedClaims()` to track progress per application.

---
id: quorum
title: Quorum
resources:
  - url: https://github.com/cartesi/rollups-contracts/tree/v3.0.0-alpha.10/src/consensus/quorum/Quorum.sol
    title: Quorum Contract
---

The **Quorum** contract implements a multi-validator consensus mechanism controlled by a small, immutable set of validators. Each validator can vote for one claim per application and epoch by submitting it. A claim is **staged** when a majority of the validators (`1 + N/2`, where `N` is the number of validators) submit the same machine Merkle root for that epoch. After the claim staging period, **anyone** can accept it through `acceptClaim()`, inherited from [`AbstractConsensus`](../abstract-consensus.md).

This contract inherits from [`IQuorum`](./iquorum.md) and [`AbstractConsensus`](../abstract-consensus.md).

## Functions

### `constructor()`

```solidity
constructor(
    address[] memory validators,
    uint256 epochLength,
    uint256 claimStagingPeriod
)
```

Each distinct validator receives an ID from 1 to `N`, in the order of the array. Duplicates in the `validators` array are ignored.

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `validators` | `address[]` | The array of validator addresses |
| `epochLength` | `uint256` | The epoch length |
| `claimStagingPeriod` | `uint256` | The claim staging period, in number of blocks |

**Errors**

| Error | Condition |
|-------|-----------|
| `ZeroEpochLength` | The epoch length is zero |
| `ZeroAddressValidator` | The `validators` array contains the zero address |
| `EmptyQuorum` | The quorum would have no validators |

### `submitClaim()`

```solidity
function submitClaim(
    address appContract,
    uint256 lastProcessedBlockNumber,
    bytes32 machineMerkleRoot,
    MachineValidityProof calldata proof
) external override
```

Submit a claim to the consensus, which counts as the caller's vote for that claim. Only validators can call this function.

The function emits `ClaimSubmitted` and registers the vote. When the vote count for the claim reaches `1 + N/2`, the claim is staged (`ClaimStaged`).

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `appContract` | `address` | The application contract address |
| `lastProcessedBlockNumber` | `uint256` | The number of the last processed block |
| `machineMerkleRoot` | `bytes32` | The post-epoch machine Merkle root |
| `proof` | `MachineValidityProof` | The machine validity proof (see [`IConsensus`](../iconsensus.md#machinevalidityproof)) |

**Errors**

| Error | Condition |
|-------|-----------|
| `CallerIsNotValidator` | The caller is not a validator |
| `NotEpochFinalBlock` | `lastProcessedBlockNumber` is not the last block of an epoch |
| `NotPastBlock` | `lastProcessedBlockNumber` is not in the past |
| `NotFirstClaim` | The caller already voted for a claim in this epoch |
| [Machine validation errors](../iconsensus.md#machine-validation-errors) | The machine validity proof is invalid |
| [Application checker errors](../iconsensus.md#application-checker-errors) | The application is not deployed, could not be checked or is foreclosed |

```solidity
) external returns (IQuorum)
```

Deploy a new quorum deterministically.

## Errors

### `ZeroEpochLength()`

```solidity
error ZeroEpochLength()
```

Raised when a consensus would be deployed with zero as epoch length. This is forbidden because it would lead to a division by zero when calculating the epoch of a block (`block.number / epochLength`).

### `ZeroAddressValidator()`

```solidity
error ZeroAddressValidator()
```

Raised when a quorum would be deployed with the zero address as one of the validators. The zero address is reserved as a sentinel value for non-validators (see `validatorById`).

### `EmptyQuorum()`

```solidity
error EmptyQuorum()
```

Raised when a quorum would be deployed with an empty array of validators.

---
id: iquorum
title: IQuorum
resources:
  - url: https://github.com/cartesi/rollups-contracts/tree/v3.0.0-alpha.10/src/consensus/quorum/IQuorum.sol
    title: IQuorum Interface
---

The `IQuorum` interface defines a consensus model controlled by a small, immutable set of validators. It inherits from [`IConsensus`](../iconsensus.md).

## Description

A consensus model controlled by a small, immutable set of `n` (at least 1) validators. You can know the value of `n` by calling the `numOfValidators` function. Upon construction, each validator is assigned a unique number between 1 and `n`. These numbers are used internally instead of addresses for gas optimization reasons. You can list the validators in the quorum by calling the `validatorById` function for each ID from 1 to `n`.

Votes are tracked per application and epoch (identified by the last processed block number), and per claim (identified by the machine Merkle root).

## Functions

### `numOfValidators`
```solidity
function numOfValidators() external view returns (uint256)
```

Get the number of validators.

**Returns:**
- (uint256): The total number of validators

**Note:** The number of validators is greater than or equal to 1.

### `validatorId`
```solidity

```

Get the ID of a validator.

**Parameters:**
- `validator` (address): The validator address

**Returns:**
- (uint256): The validator ID

**Note:** Validators have IDs greater than zero. Non-validators are assigned to ID zero.

### `validatorById`
```solidity
function validatorById(uint256 id) external view returns (address)
```

Get the address of a validator by its ID.

**Parameters:**
- `id` (uint256): The validator ID

**Returns:**
- (address): The validator address

**Note:** Validator IDs range from 1 to `N`, the total number of validators. Valid IDs do not map to address zero. Invalid IDs map to address zero.

### `numOfValidatorsInFavorOfAnyClaimInEpoch`

---
id: input-box
title: InputBox
resources:
    - url: https://github.com/cartesi/rollups-contracts/tree/v3.0.0-alpha.10/src/inputs/InputBox.sol
      title: InputBox contract
    - url: https://github.com/cartesi/rollups-contracts/tree/v3.0.0-alpha.10/src/inputs/IInputBox.sol
      title: IInputBox interface
---

The **InputBox** is a trustless and permissionless contract that receives inputs for applications from any sender. For each application, it keeps an append-only list (the "input box") of input hashes.

When an input is added, the contract wraps the sender's payload in an `EvmAdvance` envelope, which also records the chain ID, the application address, the sender, the block number, the block timestamp, `prevrandao` and the input index:

```solidity
bytes memory input = abi.encodeCall(
    Inputs.EvmAdvance,
    (block.chainid, appContract, msg.sender, block.number, block.timestamp, block.prevrandao, index, payload)
);
```

The hash stored on-chain is `keccak256(input)`, and the whole encoded `input` is emitted in the `InputAdded` event.

Data availability is guaranteed through the emission of `InputAdded` events on every successful call to `addInput`. This ensures that inputs can be retrieved by anyone at any time without relying on centralized data providers.

From this contract's perspective, payloads are encoding-agnostic byte arrays. It is the application's responsibility to interpret, validate, and act upon them.

This contract inherits from `IInputBox`, `RollupsContract` and `ApplicationChecker`.

## Choosing and checking the input box

Each application chooses its input box when it is deployed. The address is an immutable constructor argument of the [`Application`](./application.md) contract, returned by its [`getInputBox()`](./application.md#getinputbox) function. Portals deliver deposit inputs to the input box that the application reports.

Because the input box is a permissionless contract that anyone can deploy, an application can report an input box other than the canonical one. Such an input box may add inputs that do not correspond to real transactions on the canonical contracts, including deposit inputs for assets that were never transferred.

Before depositing assets into an application or relying on its outputs, users and integrators should check that the application's `getInputBox()` returns the canonical `InputBox` address of the rollups-contracts release in use. The canonical addresses are published with each release, for example in `cartesi-rollups-contracts-3.0.0-alpha.10-deployment-addresses.tar.gz` on the [v3.0.0-alpha.10 release page](https://github.com/cartesi/rollups-contracts/releases/tag/v3.0.0-alpha.10).

## State Variables

### `DEPLOYMENT_BLOCK_NUMBER`


### `_inputBoxes`
Mapping of application contract addresses to arrays of input hashes.

```solidity
mapping(address => bytes32[]) private _inputBoxes;
```

## Functions

### `addInput()`

```solidity
function addInput(address appContract, bytes calldata payload) external override notForeclosed(appContract) returns (bytes32 inputHash)
```

Send an input to an application.

*Must fire an InputAdded event.*

Before adding the input, the contract checks that `appContract` is a deployed application that is not foreclosed, by calling its `isForeclosed()` function. Inputs cannot be sent to an address with no code, such as a precomputed application address before the application is deployed.

The encoded `EvmAdvance` input, not only the payload, must fit in `CanonicalMachine.INPUT_MAX_SIZE` (65,536 bytes). Because of the envelope, the largest accepted payload is 65,216 bytes.

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `appContract` | `address` | The application contract address |
| `payload` | `bytes` | The input payload |

**Return Values**

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `inputHash` | `bytes32` | The hash of the encoded input (`keccak256` of the `EvmAdvance` envelope) |

**Errors**

| Error | Condition |
|-------|-----------|
| `ApplicationNotDeployed(address appContract)` | The application address has no code |
| `ApplicationReverted(address appContract, bytes error)` | The call to the application's `isForeclosed()` reverted |
| `IllformedApplicationReturnData(address appContract, bytes data)` | The application's `isForeclosed()` returned ill-formed data |
| `ApplicationForeclosed(address appContract)` | The application was foreclosed |
| `InputTooLarge(address appContract, uint256 inputLength, uint256 maxInputLength)` | The encoded input is larger than `maxInputLength` (65,536 bytes) |

<!-- source: https://docs.cartesi.io/cartesi-rollups/2.0/api-reference/contracts/overview/ -->

---
id: overview
title: Overview
resources:
  - url: https://github.com/cartesi/rollups-contracts/tree/v3.0.0-alpha.10
    title: Smart Contracts for Cartesi Rollups
---

The Cartesi Rollups framework consists of components on two layers: the base layer (the foundational blockchain where an application contract is deployed, such as Ethereum) and the execution layer (the Cartesi off-chain layer where the application runs its backend logic).

The frontend interacts with base layer smart contracts to send inputs to the backend, deposit assets, and process outputs.

To interact with an Ethereum-compatible blockchain, the application frontend must connect to a blockchain node using Ethereum's JSON-RPC API. 

Clients can interact with Ethereum-compatible nodes using the JSON-RPC API in two ways:

- Querying state: The state can be queried by calling functions that neither alter the blockchain state nor incur gas fees.

- Changing state: The state is changed by submitting a transaction that incurs gas fees. The transaction must be cryptographically signed by an Ethereum account with sufficient funds in its wallet.

## Cartesi Rollups Smart Contracts

- [`InputBox`](../contracts/input-box.md): This contract receives inputs from users who want to interact with the off-chain layer. Each application reads its inputs from the input box chosen at deployment, returned by the application's `getInputBox()` function. Because anyone can deploy an input box, users and integrators should check that an application's `getInputBox()` returns the canonical `InputBox` deployment before depositing into it or relying on its outputs (see [Choosing and checking the input box](../contracts/input-box.md#choosing-and-checking-the-input-box)).

- [`Application`](../contracts/application.md): This contract is instantiated for each dApp (i.e., each dApp has its own application address). With this address, an application can hold ownership of digital assets on the base layer, such as Ether, ERC-20 tokens, and NFTs.

- [`ApplicationFactory`](../contracts/application-factory.md): This contract enables anyone to deploy [`Application`](../contracts/application.md) contracts with a simple function call. It provides greater convenience to the deployer and security to users and validators, as they can verify that the bytecode has not been maliciously altered. The [`SelfHostedApplicationFactory`](../contracts/application-factory.md#selfhostedapplicationfactory) deploys an ownerless `Application` together with its `Authority` in a single transaction.

- `Portals`: These contracts are used to safely transfer assets from the base layer to the execution environment of your application. Currently, Portal contracts are available for the following types of assets: [Ether (ETH)](../contracts/portals/EtherPortal.md), [ERC-20 (Fungible tokens)](../contracts/portals/Erc20Portal.md), [ERC-721 (Non-fungible tokens)](../contracts/portals/Erc721Portal.md), [ERC-1155 single transfer](../contracts/portals/Erc1155SinglePortal.md), and [ERC-1155 batch token transfers](../contracts/portals/Erc1155BatchPortal.md). The contracts are named `EtherPortal`, `Erc20Portal`, `Erc721Portal`, `Erc1155SinglePortal` and `Erc1155BatchPortal` (the `Erc` names replaced the `ERC` ones in rollups-contracts 3.0.0-alpha.7). Each portal sends the deposit input to the input box returned by the application's `getInputBox()`.

- [`Consensus`](../contracts/consensus/overview.md): These contracts are crucial for the framework's security and integrity. They validate and stage claims submitted by validators and, after a claim staging period, accept them, ensuring the rollup's integrity by validating outputs Merkle roots. The framework supports different consensus mechanisms including [Authority-based consensus](../contracts/consensus/authority/authority.md) for single-owner control and [Quorum-based consensus](../contracts/consensus/quorum/quorum.md) for multi-validator approval. PRT applications use the `DaveConsensus` contract from the [cartesi/dave](https://github.com/cartesi/dave/tree/v3.0.0-alpha.6) repository instead (see the [consensus overview](../contracts/consensus/overview.md)).

The **Erc1155BatchPortal** allows anyone to perform batch transfers of
ERC-1155 tokens to an application contract while informing the off-chain machine.

:::note
Since rollups-contracts 3.0.0-alpha.7, this contract is named `Erc1155BatchPortal` (formerly `ERC1155BatchPortal`) and its deposit function is `depositBatchErc1155Token` (formerly `depositBatchERC1155Token`). The function selector changed, so calls encoded with the old name revert.
:::

## `depositBatchErc1155Token()`

```solidity
function depositBatchErc1155Token(IERC1155 token, address appContract, uint256[] calldata tokenIds, uint256[] calldata values, bytes calldata baseLayerData, bytes calldata execLayerData) external;
```

Transfer a batch of ERC-1155 tokens of multiple types to an application contract and add an input to
the application's input box to signal such operation.

The caller must enable approval for the portal to manage all of their tokens
beforehand, by calling the `setApprovalForAll` function in the token contract.

_Please make sure `tokenIds` and `values` have the same length._

The input is added to the input box returned by the application's `getInputBox()` function, not to a fixed input box. See the [trust note on the InputBox page](../input-box.md#choosing-and-checking-the-input-box).

If the application is foreclosed before the deposit input is finalized, anyone can call [`issueRefund()`](../application.md#issuerefund) on the application to return the tokens to the depositor. If the depositor is a smart contract, the refund only succeeds if that contract accepts the tokens through the `onERC1155Received`/`onERC1155BatchReceived` callback. Otherwise, the tokens may not be recoverable.

#### Parameters

| Name          | Type      | Description                                              |
| ------------- | --------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| token         | IERC1155  | The ERC-1155 token contract                              |
| appContract   | address   | The application contract address                         |
| tokenIds      | uint256[] | The identifiers of the tokens being transferred          |
| values        | uint256[] | Transfer amounts per token type                          |
| baseLayerData | bytes     | Additional data to be interpreted by the base layer      |
| execLayerData | bytes     | Additional data to be interpreted by the execution layer |

#### Errors

| Error | Condition |
| ----- | --------- |
| `ApplicationNotDeployed(address appContract)` | The application address has no code |
| `ApplicationReverted(address appContract, bytes error)` | The call to the application reverted |
| `IllformedApplicationReturnData(address appContract, bytes data)` | The application returned ill-formed data |
| `InputBoxNotDeployed(address inputBox)` | The input box returned by the application has no code |
| `ApplicationForeclosed(address appContract)` | The application was foreclosed (raised by the `InputBox`) |
| `InputTooLarge(address appContract, uint256 inputLength, uint256 maxInputLength)` | The encoded input exceeds the maximum input size (raised by the `InputBox`) |

Errors raised by the token contract during `safeBatchTransferFrom` (for example, a missing approval or arrays of different lengths) are propagated.

## `version()`


Get the version of the contracts project, for example `(3, 0, 0, "alpha.10", "")`. Inherited from `RollupsContract` through `Portal`.

## `depositSingleErc1155Token()`

```solidity
function depositSingleErc1155Token(IERC1155 token, address appContract, uint256 tokenId, uint256 value, bytes calldata baseLayerData, bytes calldata execLayerData) external;
```

Transfer ERC-1155 tokens of a single type to an application contract and add an input to

beforehand, by calling the `setApprovalForAll` function in the token contract.

The input is added to the input box returned by the application's `getInputBox()` function, not to a fixed input box. See the [trust note on the InputBox page](../input-box.md#choosing-and-checking-the-input-box).

If the application is foreclosed before the deposit input is finalized, anyone can call [`issueRefund()`](../application.md#issuerefund) on the application to return the tokens to the depositor. If the depositor is a smart contract, the refund only succeeds if that contract accepts the tokens through the `onERC1155Received`/`onERC1155BatchReceived` callback. Otherwise, the tokens may not be recoverable.

#### Parameters

| Name          | Type     | Description                                              |
| ------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| token         | IERC1155 | The ERC-1155 token contract                              |
| appContract   | address  | The application contract address                         |
| tokenId       | uint256  | The identifier of the token being transferred            |
| value         | uint256  | Transfer amount                                          |
| baseLayerData | bytes    | Additional data to be interpreted by the base layer      |
| execLayerData | bytes    | Additional data to be interpreted by the execution layer |

#### Errors

| Error | Condition |
| ----- | --------- |
| `ApplicationNotDeployed(address appContract)` | The application address has no code |
| `ApplicationReverted(address appContract, bytes error)` | The call to the application reverted |
| `IllformedApplicationReturnData(address appContract, bytes data)` | The application returned ill-formed data |
| `InputBoxNotDeployed(address inputBox)` | The input box returned by the application has no code |
| `ApplicationForeclosed(address appContract)` | The application was foreclosed (raised by the `InputBox`) |
| `InputTooLarge(address appContract, uint256 inputLength, uint256 maxInputLength)` | The encoded input exceeds the maximum input size (raised by the `InputBox`) |

Errors raised by the token contract during `safeTransferFrom` (for example, a missing approval) are propagated.

ERC-20 tokens to an application contract while informing the off-chain machine.

Since rollups-contracts 3.0.0-alpha.7, this contract is named `Erc20Portal` (formerly `ERC20Portal`) and its deposit function is `depositErc20Tokens` (formerly `depositERC20Tokens`). The function selector changed, so calls encoded with the old name revert.

## `depositErc20Tokens()`

```solidity
function depositErc20Tokens(IERC20 token, address appContract, uint256 value, bytes calldata execLayerData) external;
```

Transfer ERC-20 tokens to an application contract and add an input to
the application's input box to signal such operation.

The caller must allow the portal to withdraw at least `value` tokens
from their account beforehand, by calling the `approve` function in the
token contract.

Only ERC-20 compliant tokens are supported:

- The portal requires `transferFrom` to return `true`. Empty or ill-formed return values are rejected with a low-level error.
- The portal rejects fee-on-transfer tokens. It compares the application's token balance before and after the transfer and reverts unless the difference is exactly `value`.

The input is added to the input box returned by the application's `getInputBox()` function, not to a fixed input box. See the [trust note on the InputBox page](../input-box.md#choosing-and-checking-the-input-box).

If the application is foreclosed before the deposit input is finalized, anyone can call [`issueRefund()`](../application.md#issuerefund) on the application to return the tokens to the depositor.

#### Parameters

| Name          | Type    | Description                                              |
| ------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| token         | IERC20  | The ERC-20 token contract address                        |
| appContract   | address | The application contract address                         |
| value         | uint256 | The amount of tokens to be transferred                   |
| execLayerData | bytes   | Additional data to be interpreted by the execution layer |

#### Errors

| Error | Condition |
| ----- | --------- |
| `Erc20TransferFailed()` | `transferFrom` returned `false` |
| `Erc20TransferDecreasedApplicationBalance(uint256 balanceBefore, uint256 balanceAfter)` | The application's token balance decreased during the transfer |
| `Erc20TransferValueIsNotBalanceDelta(uint256 value, uint256 balanceDelta)` | The application's balance did not grow by exactly `value` (for example, a fee-on-transfer token) |
| `ApplicationNotDeployed(address appContract)` | The application address has no code |
| `ApplicationReverted(address appContract, bytes error)` | The call to the application reverted |
| `IllformedApplicationReturnData(address appContract, bytes data)` | The application returned ill-formed data |
| `InputBoxNotDeployed(address inputBox)` | The input box returned by the application has no code |
| `ApplicationForeclosed(address appContract)` | The application was foreclosed (raised by the `InputBox`) |
| `InputTooLarge(address appContract, uint256 inputLength, uint256 maxInputLength)` | The encoded input exceeds the maximum input size (raised by the `InputBox`) |

Errors raised by the token contract (for example, insufficient allowance or balance) are propagated.

---
id: iwithdrawal-output-builder
title: IWithdrawalOutputBuilder
resources:
  - url: https://github.com/cartesi/rollups-contracts/tree/v3.0.0-alpha.10/src/withdrawal/IWithdrawalOutputBuilder.sol
    title: IWithdrawalOutputBuilder interface
  - url: https://github.com/cartesi/rollups-contracts/tree/v3.0.0-alpha.10/src/withdrawal/IWithdrawalOutputBuilderErrors.sol
    title: IWithdrawalOutputBuilderErrors
---

A **withdrawal output builder** turns an account (as encoded in the application's [accounts drive](./withdrawal-config.md#drive-geometry)) into an [output](../../backend/vouchers.md) that, when executed by the [`Application`](../application.md) contract, transfers that account's funds to its owner.

During [`withdraw()`](../application.md#withdraw), the Application **static-calls** the builder set in its [`WithdrawalConfig`](./withdrawal-config.md) and runs the returned output. Because the call is a `STATICCALL`, `buildWithdrawalOutput` must not change any state (it is `view`/`pure`). Any state change, such as contract creation, log emission, storage write, self-destruct, or Ether transfer, reverts the call and aborts the withdrawal.

The account encoding is **application-specific**, with one rule every builder must follow: the account must **end with the owner's address**, as its last 20 bytes (big-endian, the usual address encoding). This lets the node look up an account by its owner in the accounts drive. A builder must not assume the account is well formed: it should check the account's length (raising [`InvalidAccountSize`](#invalidaccountsize)) and its contents. See [UsdWithdrawalOutputBuilder](./usd-withdrawal-output-builder.md) for the single-ERC-20 implementation.

## Functions

### `buildWithdrawalOutput()`

```solidity
function buildWithdrawalOutput(address appContract, bytes calldata account)
    external
    view
    returns (bytes memory output)
```

Build an output that, when executed by the application contract, transfers the funds of an account to its owner.

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `appContract` | `address` | The application contract address. May be needed for outputs that move assets from the application's own account to the account owner (e.g. ERC-721 / ERC-1155 transfers). |
| `account` | `bytes` | The account, as encoded in the accounts drive |

**Return Values**

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `output` | `bytes` | The withdrawal output |

## Errors

### `InvalidAccountSize()`

```solidity
error InvalidAccountSize(uint256 attemptedAccountSize, uint64 accountSize)
```

Raised when the provided account does not have the size the builder expects to decode on-chain. The size must match exactly.

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `attemptedAccountSize` | `uint256` | The size of the account whose funds were attempted to be withdrawn, in bytes |
| `accountSize` | `uint64` | The expected account size, in bytes |

:::note
Before rollups-contracts v3.0.0-alpha.7, this error was `AccountTooShort(uint64 attemptedAccountSize, uint64 minAccountSize)` and only enforced a minimum size.
:::

<!-- source: https://docs.cartesi.io/cartesi-rollups/2.0/api-reference/contracts/withdrawal/overview/ -->

---
id: overview
title: Overview
---

These contracts power **emergency withdrawal**: the ability for users to recover their in-app balances straight from the base layer after an application is [foreclosed](../application.md#guardian--foreclosure), without the operator's node. For the concept and the operator procedure, see [Foreclosure & Emergency Withdrawal](../../../development/emergency-withdrawal/overview.md).

Deposits whose inputs were never finalized are not part of any settled balance. They are returned through a separate path, [deposit refunds](../application.md#issuerefund), described in the [recovery guide](../../../development/emergency-withdrawal/recovery-guide.md#step-7-refund-unfinalized-deposits).

## How the pieces fit together

The withdrawal machinery lives partly on the [`Application`](../application.md) contract and partly in a small set of supporting contracts:

| Piece | Where | Role |
|-------|-------|------|
| Foreclosure + withdrawal logic | [`Application`](../application.md) (`IApplication`) | `foreclose`, `proveAccountsDriveMerkleRoot`, `withdraw`, `issueRefund`, and the account/getter views |
| [`WithdrawalConfig`](./withdrawal-config.md) | passed to the `Application` constructor | Guardian, accounts-drive geometry, and the output builder to use |
| [`IWithdrawalOutputBuilder`](./iwithdrawal-output-builder.md) | referenced by the config | Turns an account into a withdrawal output (static-called during `withdraw`) |
| [`UsdWithdrawalOutputBuilder`](./usd-withdrawal-output-builder.md) (+ [factory](./usd-withdrawal-output-builder-factory.md)) | one per ERC-20 token | The single-ERC-20 builder; builds a `DelegateCallVoucher` to the shared `SafeErc20Transfer` contract |
| [`RefundOutputBuilder`](https://github.com/cartesi/rollups-contracts/tree/v3.0.0-alpha.10/src/refund/RefundOutputBuilder.sol) | one per `ApplicationFactory`, passed to every application it deploys | Turns an unfinalized portal deposit into an output that returns the asset to its depositor (static-called during `issueRefund`) |

## The withdrawal flow, on-chain

1. The guardian calls [`foreclose()`](../application.md#foreclose) → the application is frozen at its last-finalized state.
2. Anyone calls [`proveAccountsDriveMerkleRoot()`](../application.md#proveaccountsdrivemerkleroot) once, anchoring the accounts-drive root against the finalized machine state. The application reads that state from its consensus with `getLastFinalizedMachineMerkleRoot()`: the machine root of the latest accepted claim under Authority and Quorum, or the post-epoch machine state of the latest accepted tournament result under PRT (`DaveConsensus`). If no state has been finalized yet, the consensus returns zero and the application uses its template hash instead.
3. Each user calls [`withdraw(account, proof)`](../application.md#withdraw). The Application validates the account against the anchored root, **static-calls** the configured output builder to build the transfer output, marks the account withdrawn (single-use) and emits `Withdrawal`, and then executes the output.

Separately, once the application is foreclosed, anyone can call [`issueRefund(inputIndex, input)`](../application.md#issuerefund) for a portal deposit whose input was never finalized. The refund output builder returns the asset to the original depositor.

## The four-way agreement

Emergency withdrawal only works if four descriptions of the **accounts drive** agree:

1. the **guest application** actually writes account records with the layout it claims;
2. the [`WithdrawalConfig`](./withdrawal-config.md) (`log2LeavesPerAccount`, `log2MaxNumOfAccounts`, `accountsDriveStartIndex`) matches that layout, and points at the drive the template actually reserves for the ledger;
3. the **proofs** generated off-chain (via the machine tool) use those same parameters; and
4. the **output builder** decodes the account encoding the guest produced. Every encoding must end with the owner's 20-byte address.

If any of the four disagree, proofs fail to validate or withdrawal outputs cannot be built, so these values must be chosen together at deploy time. None of this is checked at deploy time: deployment only checks that the drive fits in machine memory (see [Validation](./withdrawal-config.md#validation) and [Checking the drive position](../../backend/emergency-withdrawal.md#checking-the-drive-position)). The machine tool also supports only one layout (single-leaf, 32-byte USD records); see the [recovery guide](../../../development/emergency-withdrawal/recovery-guide.md#step-3-generate-the-proofs). See [drive geometry](./withdrawal-config.md#drive-geometry).

---

id: usd-withdrawal-output-builder-factory
title: UsdWithdrawalOutputBuilderFactory
resources:

**`UsdWithdrawalOutputBuilderFactory`** lets anyone deploy a [`UsdWithdrawalOutputBuilder`](./usd-withdrawal-output-builder.md) for a given ERC-20 token at a predictable address. Because these builders are **stateless**, it does not matter whether you deploy one yourself or reuse an existing one for the same token. The address is derived deterministically from the token and salt (using `CREATE2`).

The factory is constructed with a shared [`SafeErc20Transfer`](https://github.com/cartesi/rollups-contracts/tree/v3.0.0-alpha.10/src/delegatecall/SafeErc20Transfer.sol) contract, which it passes to every builder it deploys (used as the delegate-call voucher destination). Before rollups-contracts v3.0.0-alpha.7, this contract and its interface were named `SafeERC20Transfer` and `ISafeERC20Transfer`.

<!-- source: https://docs.cartesi.io/cartesi-rollups/2.0/api-reference/contracts/withdrawal/usd-withdrawal-output-builder/ -->

---
id: usd-withdrawal-output-builder
title: UsdWithdrawalOutputBuilder
resources:
  - url: https://github.com/cartesi/rollups-contracts/tree/v3.0.0-alpha.10/src/withdrawal/UsdWithdrawalOutputBuilder.sol
    title: UsdWithdrawalOutputBuilder contract
  - url: https://github.com/cartesi/rollups-contracts/tree/v3.0.0-alpha.10/src/withdrawal/IUsdWithdrawalOutputBuilder.sol
    title: IUsdWithdrawalOutputBuilder interface
---

**`UsdWithdrawalOutputBuilder`** is a concrete [`IWithdrawalOutputBuilder`](./iwithdrawal-output-builder.md) for applications whose accounts drive denominates a **single ERC-20 token**. It is a stateless contract fixed to one token at construction; deploy one per token with the [factory](./usd-withdrawal-output-builder-factory.md).

For each account it produces a **`DelegateCallVoucher`** that delegate-calls a shared [`SafeErc20Transfer`](https://github.com/cartesi/rollups-contracts/tree/v3.0.0-alpha.10/src/delegatecall/SafeErc20Transfer.sol) contract to move `balance` of the token to the account owner. (Before rollups-contracts v3.0.0-alpha.7, this contract and its interface were named `SafeERC20Transfer` and `ISafeERC20Transfer`.)

## Account encoding

The builder decodes each account with `LibUsdAccount`. An account is **exactly 32 bytes**, with no padding:

| Bytes | Content |
|-------|---------|
| `0` to `11` | The balance, a `uint96` stored **little-endian** (at most `2^96 - 1`) |
| `12` to `31` | The owner address (20 bytes, big-endian) |

For example, a balance of `1000` (`0x3e8`) owned by `0xbd8eba8bf9e56ad92f4c4fc89d6cb88902535749` is encoded as `0xe80300000000000000000000bd8eba8bf9e56ad92f4c4fc89d6cb88902535749`.

:::caution
Before rollups-contracts v3.0.0-alpha.7, the balance was a `uint64` in bytes `0` to `7` and the owner was in bytes `8` to `27`. A record written in that older layout still has a valid proof, but this builder decodes it to a different owner and balance. Make sure the guest writes the layout above.
:::

### `buildWithdrawalOutput()`

```solidity
function buildWithdrawalOutput(address, bytes calldata account)
    external
    view
    override
    returns (bytes memory output)
```

Decode `account` (see [Account encoding](#account-encoding)) into the owner `user` and its `balance`, and return a `DelegateCallVoucher` that, when executed by the application, calls `SafeErc20Transfer.safeTransfer(token, user, balance)`.

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `account` | `bytes` | The account, decoded via `LibUsdAccount.decode` into `(address user, uint96 balance)` |

**Return Values**

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `output` | `bytes` | An ABI-encoded `DelegateCallVoucher(destination, payload)` where `destination` is the `SafeErc20Transfer` contract and `payload` is `safeTransfer(token, user, balance)` |

*Raises [`InvalidAccountSize`](./iwithdrawal-output-builder.md#invalidaccountsize) if the account is not exactly 32 bytes long.*

title: WithdrawalConfig
resources:
  - url: https://github.com/cartesi/rollups-contracts/tree/v3.0.0-alpha.10/src/common/WithdrawalConfig.sol
    title: WithdrawalConfig struct
  - url: https://github.com/cartesi/rollups-contracts/tree/v3.0.0-alpha.10/src/library/LibWithdrawalConfig.sol
    title: LibWithdrawalConfig library
---

The **`WithdrawalConfig`** struct is passed to the [`Application`](../application.md#constructor) constructor to enable **foreclosure and emergency withdrawal**. It defines who may foreclose the application (the **guardian**), the geometry of the **accounts drive** (the in-app balance ledger held inside the machine state), and the contract that builds withdrawal outputs.

A **zero-valued** `WithdrawalConfig` is valid and deploys an application **without** the feature. With the Cartesi Rollups CLI, deploy without the feature by omitting `--withdrawal-config-file` (and `--withdrawal-config`): the CLI rejects a config with a zero guardian or a zero output builder.

## Struct

```solidity
struct WithdrawalConfig {
    address guardian;
    uint8 log2LeavesPerAccount;
    uint8 log2MaxNumOfAccounts;
    uint64 accountsDriveStartIndex;
    IWithdrawalOutputBuilder withdrawalOutputBuilder;
}
```

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `guardian` | `address` | The account allowed to call [`foreclose()`](../application.md#foreclose). |
| `log2LeavesPerAccount` | `uint8` | Log2 of the machine-state-tree leaves reserved per account. Each account record occupies `2^(5 + log2LeavesPerAccount)` bytes. |
| `log2MaxNumOfAccounts` | `uint8` | Log2 of the maximum number of accounts. This is the depth of the accounts-drive tree. |
| `accountsDriveStartIndex` | `uint64` | Start-index factor that positions the accounts drive in machine memory (see [Drive geometry](#drive-geometry)). |
| `withdrawalOutputBuilder` | `IWithdrawalOutputBuilder` | The contract that builds the withdrawal output for an account. See [IWithdrawalOutputBuilder](./iwithdrawal-output-builder.md). |

## Drive geometry

Let `a = log2LeavesPerAccount`, `b = log2MaxNumOfAccounts`, and `c = accountsDriveStartIndex`. The accounts drive:

- has a **size** of `2^(a + b + 5)` bytes (the `+5` is the log2 of the 32-byte data block, `CanonicalMachine.LOG2_DATA_BLOCK_SIZE`);
- **starts** at machine memory address `c * 2^(a + b + 5)`;
- holds up to `2^b` accounts, each occupying `2^(a + 5)` bytes.

These same three values are returned on-chain by [`getLog2LeavesPerAccount()`](../application.md#getlog2leavesperaccount), [`getLog2MaxNumOfAccounts()`](../application.md#getlog2maxnumofaccounts), and [`getAccountsDriveStartIndex()`](../application.md#getaccountsdrivestartindex), and must match the layout the guest application actually writes.

## Validation

```solidity
function isValid(WithdrawalConfig memory withdrawalConfig) internal pure returns (bool)
```

The `Application` constructor calls `isValid()` and reverts with `InvalidWithdrawalConfig` (see [ApplicationFactory](../application-factory.md#invalidwithdrawalconfig)) if it returns `false`. `isValid()` enforces that the accounts drive fits inside the machine memory:

- `log2(driveSize) = 5 + log2MaxNumOfAccounts + log2LeavesPerAccount` must not exceed `64` (the machine memory is `2^64` bytes); and
- the drive's end address `(accountsDriveStartIndex + 1) << log2(driveSize)` must not overflow and must not exceed `2^64`.

:::warning
`isValid()` does **not** check that the config points at the template's accounts drive, and neither does the Cartesi Rollups CLI. A config whose start index or sizes are wrong deploys without error, but withdrawals and proofs then read whatever machine memory it selects. Check the drive position against the machine template before deploying; see [Checking the drive position](../../backend/emergency-withdrawal.md#checking-the-drive-position).
:::

:::note
`isValid()` checks only the **drive geometry**. It does **not** reject a zero `guardian` or a zero `withdrawalOutputBuilder`. A config with those set to zero still passes the constructor, as long as its geometry is valid. Deployment tools such as the Cartesi Rollups CLI go further and refuse a zero guardian or builder for an *enabled* config, but a direct factory call would not.
:::

API that allows the application frontend to make inspect-state requests to the application backend
through a Cartesi Rollups node.

This reference describes the inspect server of rollups-node v2.0.0-alpha.14.
The node serves it on the address set by `CARTESI_INSPECT_ADDRESS` (default `:10012`).
With `cartesi run`, the CLI devnet serves it at `http://127.0.0.1:6751/inspect/<application>`.
CORS is disabled by default; to call the API from a browser, the node operator must list the
allowed origins in `CARTESI_INSPECT_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`.

<Heading
  as={"h1"}
  className={"openapi__heading"}
  children={"Inspect application state"}
>
</Heading>

<MethodEndpoint
  method={"post"}
  path={"/inspect/{application}"}
  context={"endpoint"}
>
  
</MethodEndpoint>



This method sends an inspect-state request to the application backend. The request body is
passed to the backend unchanged, as the raw bytes of the inspect payload. The node does not
interpret the body or its content type. The body can be at most 2 MiB (the size of the
Cartesi Machine CMIO RX buffer); larger bodies are rejected with HTTP 413.

Only `POST` is accepted. Other HTTP methods receive HTTP 405 with an `Allow: POST` header.

The node runs the request on a fork of the application's current machine state, so the
inspect cannot change the application state. `processed_input_count` tells how many inputs
that state includes. Inspect requests run concurrently: each application accepts up to its
`max_concurrent_inspects` execution parameter (default 10) at a time, and the whole inspect
server accepts up to `CARTESI_INSPECT_MAX_INFLIGHT` requests (default 64). Requests beyond
these limits are rejected with HTTP 503 instead of waiting in a queue.

A successful request returns HTTP 200 with a JSON body. The `status` field tells how the
inspection ended:
- `Accepted`: the backend accepted the request.
- `Rejected`: the backend rejected the request.
- `Exception`: the backend raised an exception. `exception_data` holds the exception
  payload, and `error` holds a fixed message.
- `MachineHalted`: the machine halted while processing the request.
- `Failed`: the node could not complete the inspection, for example because a cycle or time
  limit was reached. `error` holds a fixed message; details are only in the node logs.

`reports` holds the reports that the backend emitted, including the ones emitted before a
failure. Inspect reports are returned only in this response: the node does not store them,
so they are not available through the JSON-RPC API.

# JSON-RPC API Methods

This page provides a quick reference to all available JSON-RPC methods in the Cartesi Rollups Node API (rollups-node v2.0.0-alpha.14). For each method, you will find:
- A summary of what it does
- The parameters it accepts (with types and descriptions)
- **Links to detailed documentation for each method**

Use this as a starting point to explore the API. For more details on each method, see the dedicated documentation pages in the sidebar or follow the links below. For error codes and limits that apply to every method, see the [Overview](./overview.md#error-handling).

Common rules for list methods:
- `limit` (optional): Maximum number of items to return per page. Default: 50. An omitted `limit` or 0 selects the default; values above 10000 are capped at 10000.
- `offset` (optional): Starting point of the page. Default: 0, Minimum: 0.
- `descending` (optional): If `true`, sort in descending order. Default: `false`.

Integer parameters (indexes, `from`, `to`) are hex encoded strings, for example `"0x1a"`.

## Applications

### [cartesi_listApplications](./methods/applications/list.md)
Returns a paginated list of all applications registered in the node.

Parameters:
- `limit`, `offset` (optional): Pagination.
- `descending` (optional): Sort by application name in descending order.

### [cartesi_getApplication](./methods/applications/get.md)
Fetches detailed information about a specific application by its name or address.

Parameters:
- `application` (required): The application's name or hex encoded address.

## Epochs

### [cartesi_listEpochs](./methods/epochs/list.md)
Returns a paginated list of epochs for a given application. Proofs are omitted from the listed epochs.

Parameters:
- `application` (required): The application's name or hex encoded address.
- `status` (optional): Filter by one epoch status, or by a non-empty list of statuses.
- `from`, `to` (optional): Inclusive lower and upper bounds on the epoch index (hex encoded).
- `limit`, `offset` (optional): Pagination.
- `descending` (optional): Sort by epoch index in descending order.

### [cartesi_getEpoch](./methods/epochs/get.md)
Fetches detailed information about a specific epoch.

Parameters:
- `application` (required): The application's name or hex encoded address.
- `epoch_index` (required): The index of the epoch to be retrieved (hex encoded).

### [cartesi_getEpochByVirtualIndex](./methods/epochs/get-by-virtual-index.md)
Fetches an epoch by its virtual index, the epoch's dense insertion rank (0, 1, 2, … without gaps).

Parameters:
- `application` (required): The application's name or hex encoded address.
- `virtual_index` (required): The virtual index of the epoch (hex encoded).

### [cartesi_getLastAcceptedEpochIndex](./methods/epochs/last-accepted.md)
Fetches the latest accepted epoch index for a given application.

Parameters:
- `application` (required): The application's name or hex encoded address.

## Inputs

### [cartesi_listInputs](./methods/inputs/list.md)
Returns a paginated list of inputs sent to an application.

Parameters:
- `application` (required): The application's name or hex encoded address.
- `epoch_index` (optional): Filter inputs by a specific epoch index (hex encoded).
- `sender` (optional): Filter inputs by the sender's address (hex encoded).
- `transaction_hash` (optional): Filter inputs by the L1 transaction hash that emitted the `InputAdded` event.
- `from`, `to` (optional): Inclusive lower and upper bounds on the input index (hex encoded).
- `limit`, `offset` (optional): Pagination.
- `descending` (optional): Sort by input index in descending order.

### [cartesi_getInput](./methods/inputs/get.md)
Retrieves detailed information about a specific input.

Parameters:
- `application` (required): The application's name or hex encoded address.
- `input_index` (required): The index of the input to be retrieved (hex encoded).

### [cartesi_getProcessedInputCount](./methods/inputs/processed-count.md)
Returns the number of inputs already processed by the application.

Parameters:
- `application` (required): The application's name or hex encoded address.

## Outputs

### [cartesi_listOutputs](./methods/outputs/list.md)
Returns a paginated list of outputs (notices, vouchers, DELEGATECALL vouchers) for a given application.

Parameters:
- `application` (required): The application's name or hex encoded address.
- `epoch_index` (optional): Filter outputs by a specific epoch index (hex encoded).
- `input_index` (optional): Filter outputs by a specific input index (hex encoded).
- `output_type` (optional): Filter outputs by one output type selector (first 4 bytes of raw data, hex encoded) or by a non-empty list of selectors.
- `voucher_address` (optional): Filter outputs by the voucher address (hex encoded).
- `executed` (optional): `true` selects outputs with an execution transaction hash, `false` selects outputs without one.
- `from`, `to` (optional): Inclusive lower and upper bounds on the output index (hex encoded).
- `limit`, `offset` (optional): Pagination.
- `descending` (optional): Sort by output index in descending order.

### [cartesi_getOutput](./methods/outputs/get.md)
Retrieves detailed information about a specific output.

Parameters:
- `application` (required): The application's name or hex encoded address.
- `output_index` (required): The index of the output to be retrieved (hex encoded).

### [cartesi_getExecutedOutputCount](./methods/outputs/executed-count.md)
Returns the number of outputs whose on-chain execution the node has observed. Use it as a change signal for output execution.

Parameters:
- `application` (required): The application's name or hex encoded address.

### [cartesi_getPendingExecutableOutputCount](./methods/outputs/pending-executable-count.md)
Returns the number of vouchers and DELEGATECALL vouchers that have not been executed.

Parameters:
- `application` (required): The application's name or hex encoded address.

## Reports

### [cartesi_listReports](./methods/reports/list.md)
Returns a paginated list of reports for a given application.

Parameters:
- `application` (required): The application's name or hex encoded address.
- `epoch_index` (optional): Filter by epoch index (hex encoded).
- `input_index` (optional): Filter by input index (hex encoded).
- `from`, `to` (optional): Inclusive lower and upper bounds on the report index (hex encoded).
- `limit`, `offset` (optional): Pagination.
- `descending` (optional): Sort by report index in descending order.

### [cartesi_getReport](./methods/reports/get.md)
Fetches detailed information about a specific report.

Parameters:
- `application` (required): The application's name or hex encoded address.
- `report_index` (required): The index of the report to be retrieved (hex encoded).

## Emergency Withdrawals

### [cartesi_listWithdrawals](./methods/withdrawals/list.md)
Returns a paginated list of the `Withdrawal` events observed for a foreclosed application.

Parameters:
- `application` (required): The application's name or hex encoded address.
- `account_index` (optional): Filter by account index (hex encoded).
- `limit`, `offset` (optional): Pagination.
- `descending` (optional): Sort by account index in descending order.

### [cartesi_getWithdrawal](./methods/withdrawals/get.md)
Fetches a single `Withdrawal` event by application and account index.

Parameters:
- `application` (required): The application's name or hex encoded address.
- `account_index` (required): The account index of the withdrawal (hex encoded).

## PRT (Dave) Tournaments

These methods expose the dispute data that the node indexes for applications that use PRT consensus: tournaments, the commitments that joined them, matches between commitments, match advances, bond events and tournament standing changes. Tournaments, commitments and matches also carry a `snapshot` of the current contract state, read at the block given in its `as_of_block` field. The complete result schemas are part of the OpenRPC document returned by `rpc.discover`. All methods take `application` (required, name or hex encoded address), and all list methods take `limit`, `offset` and `descending`.

| Method | Additional parameters | Returns |
|--------|-----------------------|---------|
| `cartesi_listTournaments` | `epoch_index`, `level`, `parent_tournament_address`, `parent_match_id_hash` (all optional) | Paginated list of tournaments |
| `cartesi_getTournament` | `address` (required) | One tournament |
| `cartesi_listCommitments` | `epoch_index`, `tournament_address` (optional) | Paginated list of commitments |
| `cartesi_getCommitment` | `epoch_index`, `tournament_address`, `commitment` (required) | One commitment |
| `cartesi_listMatches` | `epoch_index`, `tournament_address` (optional) | Paginated list of matches |
| `cartesi_getMatch` | `epoch_index`, `tournament_address`, `id_hash` (required) | One match |
| `cartesi_listMatchAdvances` | `epoch_index`, `tournament_address`, `id_hash` (required) | Paginated list of advances of one match, ordered by block number and log index |
| `cartesi_getMatchAdvance` | `epoch_index`, `tournament_address`, `id_hash`, `tx_hash`, `log_index` (required) | One match advance |
| `cartesi_listBondEvents` | `epoch_index`, `tournament_address` (optional) | Paginated list of partial bond refunds and bond recoveries, ordered by block number and log index |
| `cartesi_getBondEvent` | `tx_hash`, `log_index` (required) | One bond event |
| `cartesi_listStandingChanges` | `epoch_index`, `tournament_address` (required) | Paginated list of the `StandingChanged` events of one tournament, ordered by block number and log index. Use `descending: true` and `limit: 1` to get the latest one |
| `cartesi_getStandingChange` | `epoch_index`, `tournament_address`, `tx_hash`, `log_index` (required) | One standing change |

The `get` methods return error `-31001` when the requested object does not exist.

## Node Information

### [cartesi_getNodeInfo](./methods/node/node-info.md)
Fetches the chain ID, the node version and the default block tag (finality level) that the node uses for chain data.

No parameters required.

### [cartesi_getChainId](./methods/node/chain-id.md) (deprecated)
Fetches the chain ID that the node is operating on. Use `cartesi_getNodeInfo` instead.

No parameters required.

### [cartesi_getNodeVersion](./methods/node/version.md) (deprecated)
Fetches the semantic version of the Cartesi rollups node. Use `cartesi_getNodeInfo` instead.

No parameters required.

### rpc.discover
Returns the OpenRPC document that describes every method, parameter, result and error of the API.

No parameters required.

# Get Application

## Example Request

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "method": "cartesi_getApplication",
  "params": {
    "application": "<name-or-address>"
  },
  "id": 1
}
```

The `cartesi_getApplication` method retrieves detailed information about a specific application by its name or address.

## Parameters

| Name          | Type   | Required | Description                                      |
|---------------|--------|----------|--------------------------------------------------|
| application   | string | Yes      | The application's name or hex encoded address    |

### Response Fields

| Name                    | Type   | Description                                      |
|-------------------------|--------|--------------------------------------------------|
| name                    | string | The name of the application                      |
| iapplication_address    | string | The Ethereum address of the application contract |
| iconsensus_address      | string | The Ethereum address of the consensus contract   |
| iinputbox_address       | string | The Ethereum address of the input box contract the application uses |
| template_hash           | string | The hash of the application template             |
| epoch_length            | string | The length of each epoch in blocks (hex encoded) |
| claim_staging_period    | string | The claim staging period in blocks (hex encoded) |
| withdrawal_config       | object | The emergency withdrawal configuration (all zero when not configured). See [WithdrawalConfig](../../types.md#withdrawalconfig) |
| consensus_type          | string | `AUTHORITY`, `QUORUM` or `PRT`                   |
| enabled                 | boolean | Operator intent: `true` if the node should keep observing and processing the application |
| status                  | string | Whether the node can still execute the application: `OK`, `FAILED`, `DIVERGED`, `CORRUPTED`, `GUEST_EXCEPTION`, `MACHINE_HALTED`, `MCYCLE_OVERFLOW`, `UNEXPECTED_YIELD` or `INVALID_OUTPUTS_ROOT`. Only `OK` and `FAILED` are not terminal. See [ApplicationStatus](../../types.md#applicationstatus) |
| reason                  | string \| null | Description of the failure. Always set when `status` is not `OK`; `null` when `status` is `OK` |
| iinputbox_block         | string | The deployment block of the input box contract; the node reads inputs from this block on |
| last_epoch_check_block  | string | The last block checked for epochs                |
| last_input_check_block  | string | The last block checked for inputs                |
| last_output_check_block | string | The last block checked for output executions     |
| last_tournament_check_block | string | The last block checked for PRT tournaments   |
| last_foreclose_check_block | string | The last block checked for a foreclosure      |
| last_accounts_drive_proved_check_block | string | The last block checked for the accounts drive proof (foreclosed applications only) |
| last_withdrawal_check_block | string | The last block checked for withdrawals (after the accounts drive is proved) |
| processed_inputs        | string | The number of processed inputs                   |
| foreclose_block         | string | The block of the on-chain foreclosure, or `0x0` if the node has not observed one |
| foreclose_transaction   | string \| null | The foreclosure transaction hash, or `null`      |
| accounts_drive_proved_block | string | The block in which the accounts drive was proved, or `0x0` |
| accounts_drive_proved_transaction | string \| null | The transaction that proved the accounts drive, or `null` |
| accounts_drive_merkle_root | string \| null | The proved accounts drive Merkle root, or `null` |
| created_at              | string | Timestamp when the application was created       |
| updated_at              | string | Timestamp when the application was last updated  |
| execution_parameters    | object | Configuration parameters for application execution |

A running application has `enabled: true` and `status: "OK"`. To tell a recoverable failure from a permanent one, check `status`: `FAILED` can be cleared by the operator, while the other non-`OK` statuses are terminal.

#### Execution Parameters

| Name                    | Type   | Description                                      |
|-------------------------|--------|--------------------------------------------------|
| snapshot_policy         | string | The snapshot policy (NONE/EVERY_INPUT/EVERY_EPOCH) |
| advance_inc_cycles      | string | Incremental cycles for advance state             |
| advance_max_cycles      | string | Maximum cycles for advance state                 |
| inspect_inc_cycles      | string | Incremental cycles for inspect state             |
| inspect_max_cycles      | string | Maximum cycles for inspect state                 |
| advance_inc_deadline    | string | Incremental deadline for advance state (ns)      |
| advance_max_deadline    | string | Maximum deadline for advance state (ns)          |
| inspect_inc_deadline    | string | Incremental deadline for inspect state (ns)      |
| inspect_max_deadline    | string | Maximum deadline for inspect state (ns)          |
| load_deadline          | string | Deadline for loading state (ns)                  |
| store_deadline         | string | Deadline for storing state (ns)                  |
| fast_deadline          | string | Deadline for fast operations (ns)                |
| max_concurrent_inspects| number | Maximum number of concurrent inspect operations  |
| created_at             | string | Timestamp when parameters were created           |
| updated_at             | string | Timestamp when parameters were last updated      |

## Error Codes

| Code    | Message                      | Description                                      |
|---------|------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| -32602  | Invalid parameters           | Invalid parameter values                         |
| -31002  | Application not found        | The node does not know the application. Retrying does not help |
| -32603  | Internal server error        | A node-side error occurred                       |
| -32070  | Request timed out            | The request could not be processed in time       |
| -31003  | Response size limit exceeded | The response exceeds the response size budget    |

title: Get Epoch by Virtual Index

# Get Epoch by Virtual Index

## Example Request

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "method": "cartesi_getEpochByVirtualIndex",
  "params": {
    "application": "<name-or-address>",
    "virtual_index": "<hex-encoded-index>"
  },
  "id": 1
}
```

The `cartesi_getEpochByVirtualIndex` method retrieves an epoch by its virtual index. The virtual index is the epoch's dense insertion rank in the node: 0, 1, 2, … without gaps by construction. Use it to walk all epochs of an application one by one, independently of the epoch index values.

## Parameters

| Name          | Type   | Required | Description                                      |
|---------------|--------|----------|--------------------------------------------------|
| application   | string | Yes      | The application's name or hex encoded address    |
| virtual_index | string | Yes      | The virtual index of the epoch to be retrieved (hex encoded) |

## Response

The response has the same format as [`cartesi_getEpoch`](./get.md#response), including the proof lists.

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "result": {
    "data": {
      "index": "0x1",
      "first_block": "0x101",
      "last_block": "0x200",
      "input_index_lower_bound": "0x1",
      "input_index_upper_bound": "0x3",
      "machine_hash": null,
      "tx_buffer_data_block": null,
      "iflags_y_data_block": null,
      "htif_tohost_data_block": null,
      "claim_transaction_hash": null,
      "commitment": null,
      "tournament_address": null,
      "status": "CLOSED",
      "staged_at_block": null,
      "virtual_index": "0x1",
      "created_at": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "updated_at": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    }
  },
  "id": 1
}
```

For the description of each field and of the epoch statuses, see [Get Epoch](./get.md#response-fields).

## Error Codes

| Code    | Message                      | Description                                      |
|---------|------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| -32602  | Invalid parameters           | Invalid parameter values                         |
| -31002  | Application not found        | The node does not know the application. Retrying does not help |
| -31001  | Epoch not found              | The application exists but no epoch has this virtual index yet. Safe to poll for the next virtual index |
| -32603  | Internal server error        | A node-side error occurred                       |
| -32070  | Request timed out            | The request could not be processed in time       |
| -31003  | Response size limit exceeded | The response exceeds the response size budget    |

# Get Epoch

## Example Request

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "method": "cartesi_getEpoch",
  "params": {
    "application": "<name-or-address>",
    "epoch_index": "<hex-encoded-index>"
  },
  "id": 1
}
```

The `cartesi_getEpoch` method retrieves detailed information about a specific epoch by its application and index.

## Parameters

| Name        | Type   | Required | Description                                      |
|-------------|--------|----------|--------------------------------------------------|
| application | string | Yes      | The application's name or hex encoded address    |
| epoch_index | string | Yes      | The index of the epoch to be retrieved (hex encoded) |

## Response

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "result": {
    "data": {
      "index": "0x1",
      "first_block": "0x101",
      "last_block": "0x200",
      "input_index_lower_bound": "0x1",
      "input_index_upper_bound": "0x3",
      "machine_hash": "0x1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef",
      "tx_buffer_data_block": "0x1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef",
      "tx_buffer_proof": [
        "0x1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef"
      ],
      "iflags_y_data_block": "0x1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef",
      "iflags_y_proof": [
        "0x1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef"
      ],
      "htif_tohost_data_block": "0x1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef",
      "htif_tohost_proof": [
        "0x1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef"
      ],
      "claim_transaction_hash": "0x1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef",
      "commitment": null,
      "tournament_address": null,
      "status": "CLAIM_ACCEPTED",
      "staged_at_block": "0x205",
      "virtual_index": "0x1",
      "created_at": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "updated_at": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    }
  },
  "id": 1
}
```

The proof lists are shortened in this example.

### Response Fields

| Name                    | Type   | Description                                      |
|-------------------------|--------|--------------------------------------------------|
| index                   | string | The epoch index (hex encoded)                    |
| first_block             | string | The first block number of the epoch (hex encoded) |
| last_block              | string | The last block number of the epoch (hex encoded)  |
| input_index_lower_bound | string | Index of the first input of the epoch (inclusive, hex encoded) |
| input_index_upper_bound | string | Index after the last input of the epoch (exclusive, hex encoded) |
| machine_hash            | string \| null | The machine state hash at the end of the epoch. Until the epoch reaches `INPUTS_PROCESSED`, the state after the last of its inputs processed so far (null until one is processed) |
| tx_buffer_data_block    | string \| null | The CMIO TX buffer data block of the machine state |
| tx_buffer_proof         | array  | Sibling hashes proving `tx_buffer_data_block` against `machine_hash` (omitted when absent) |
| iflags_y_data_block     | string \| null | The memory block that holds the machine `iflags.Y` register |
| iflags_y_proof          | array  | Sibling hashes proving `iflags_y_data_block` against `machine_hash` (omitted when absent) |
| htif_tohost_data_block  | string \| null | The memory block that holds the machine HTIF `tohost` register |
| htif_tohost_proof       | array  | Sibling hashes proving `htif_tohost_data_block` against `machine_hash` (omitted when absent) |
| claim_transaction_hash  | string \| null | The transaction hash associated with the epoch claim (null if none yet) |
| commitment              | string \| null | PRT only: the node's commitment for the epoch tournament |
| commitment_proof        | array  | PRT only: proof of the commitment (omitted when absent) |
| tournament_address      | string \| null | PRT only: the address of the epoch tournament |
| status                  | string | Current status of the epoch. See [Epoch statuses](#epoch-statuses) |
| staged_at_block         | string \| null | The block in which the claim was staged on chain (null before staging) |
| virtual_index           | string | The virtual index of the epoch: its dense insertion rank (hex encoded) |
| created_at              | string | Timestamp when the epoch was created             |
| updated_at              | string | Timestamp when the epoch was last updated        |

### Epoch statuses

| Status             | Meaning | Terminal |
|--------------------|---------|----------|
| `OPEN`             | The epoch is open and accepting inputs | No |
| `CLOSED`           | The epoch is closed and not accepting inputs | No |
| `INPUTS_PROCESSED` | The epoch inputs have been processed | No |
| `CLAIM_COMPUTED`   | The node computed the claim and the output proofs | No |
| `CLAIM_SUBMITTED`  | The node submitted the claim on chain | No |
| `CLAIM_STAGED`     | The claim (for PRT, the tournament result) is staged on chain and waits for the claim staging period to end; for PRT, it can also be accepted earlier, when all sentries agree | No |
| `CLAIM_ACCEPTED`   | The claim was accepted on chain. The epoch's outputs can now be executed | Yes |
| `CLAIM_REJECTED`   | Another claim for this epoch was staged or accepted on chain (Quorum) | Yes |
| `CLAIM_FORECLOSED` | The application was foreclosed before the claim was accepted. The claim will never be accepted | Yes |

Only `CLAIM_ACCEPTED` makes the epoch's outputs executable on chain. The node returns output proofs from `CLAIM_COMPUTED` on, but an `executeOutput` call made before the claim is accepted reverts. See [Get Output](../outputs/get.md#proofs-and-executability).

## Error Codes

| Code    | Message                      | Description                                      |
|---------|------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| -32602  | Invalid parameters           | Invalid parameter values                         |
| -31002  | Application not found        | The node does not know the application. Retrying does not help |
| -31001  | Epoch not found              | The application exists but the epoch does not. For an epoch index that may still be created, this is safe to poll |
| -32603  | Internal server error        | A node-side error occurred                       |
| -32070  | Request timed out            | The request could not be processed in time       |
| -31003  | Response size limit exceeded | The response exceeds the response size budget    |
