---
id: erc-721-token-wallet
title: Integrating ERC721 token wallet functionality
---

This tutorial will guide you through creating a basic ERC721(NFT) token wallet using TypeScript for a Cartesi backend application.

## Setting up the project

First, set up your Cartesi project as described in the [Ether wallet tutorial](./ether-wallet.md#setting-up-the-project): create a new TypeScript project, install [`viem`](https://viem.sh/) as a development dependency and let rolldown bundle it:

```bash
cartesi create erc-721-token-wallet --template typescript
cd erc-721-token-wallet
pnpm add -D viem@2.57.19
```

Then replace the contents of `rolldown.config.ts` with the configuration shown in the [Ether wallet tutorial](./ether-wallet.md#setting-up-the-project), which sets `external: ["@cartesi/rollup"]`.

ERC-721 deposit payloads use packed fields (`token`, `sender`, `tokenId`) with an optional standard-ABI tail; see [asset handling](../development/asset-handling.md#abi-encoding-for-deposits). Withdrawals emit vouchers whose `safeTransferFrom` sender is your on-chain application address (`request.appContract` on each advance request)—see [withdrawing tokens](../development/asset-handling.md#withdrawing-tokens).

## Building the ERC721 wallet

Create a file named `balance.ts` in the `src/wallet` directory and add the following code:

```typescript
import type { Address } from "viem";

export class Balance {
  private account: string;
  private erc721Tokens: Map<Address, Set<number>>;

  constructor(account: string, erc721Tokens: Map<Address, Set<number>>) {
    this.account = account;
    this.erc721Tokens = erc721Tokens;
  }

  listErc721(): Map<Address, Set<number>> {
    return this.erc721Tokens;
  }

  getErc721Tokens(erc721: Address): Set<number> | undefined {
    return this.erc721Tokens.get(erc721);
  }

  addErc721Token(erc721: Address, tokenId: number): void {
    if (!this.erc721Tokens.has(erc721)) {
      this.erc721Tokens.set(erc721, new Set());
    }
    const tokens = this.erc721Tokens.get(erc721);
    if (tokens) {
      tokens.add(tokenId);
    } else {
      throw new Error(
        `Failed to add token ${erc721}, id:${tokenId} for ${this.account}`,
      );
    }
  }

  removeErc721Token(erc721: Address, tokenId: number): void {
    if (!this.erc721Tokens.has(erc721)) {
      throw new Error(
        `Failed to remove token ${erc721}, id:${tokenId} from ${this.account}: Collection not found`,
      );
    }
    const tokens = this.erc721Tokens.get(erc721);
    if (!tokens?.delete(tokenId)) {
      throw new Error(
        `Failed to remove token ${erc721}, id:${tokenId} from ${this.account}: Token not found`,
      );
    }
  }
}
```

The `Balance` class represents an account's balance. It contains a map of ERC721 tokens and their corresponding token IDs.

Now, create a file named `wallet.ts` in the `src/wallet` directory and add the following code:

```typescript
import type { Voucher } from "@cartesi/rollup";
import {
  type Address,
  encodeFunctionData,
  erc721Abi,
  getAddress,
  type Hex,
  sliceHex,
} from "viem";
import { Balance } from "./balance";

export class Wallet {
  private accounts: Map<Address, Balance> = new Map();

  private getOrCreateBalance(address: Address): Balance {
    const key = getAddress(address);
    let balance = this.accounts.get(key);
    if (!balance) {
      balance = new Balance(key, new Map());
      this.accounts.set(key, balance);
    }
    return balance;
  }

  getBalance(address: Address): Balance {
    return this.getOrCreateBalance(address);
  }

  getErc721Balance(
    address: Address,
    erc721: Address,
  ): { address: string; erc721: string; tokenIds: number[] } {
    const balance = this.getOrCreateBalance(address);
    const tokens = balance.getErc721Tokens(erc721) || new Set<number>();
    const tokenIdsArray = Array.from(tokens);

    const result = {
      address: address,
      erc721: erc721,
      tokenIds: tokenIdsArray,
    };

    console.info(
      `ERC721 balance for ${address} and contract ${erc721}: ${JSON.stringify(result)}`,
    );
    return result;
  }

  processErc721Deposit(payload: Hex): string {
    const [erc721, account, tokenId] = this.parseErc721Deposit(payload);
    console.info(
      `Token ERC-721 ${erc721} id: ${tokenId} deposited in ${account}`,
    );
    return this.depositErc721(account, erc721, tokenId);
  }

  private parseErc721Deposit(payload: Hex): [Address, Address, number] {
    const erc721 = getAddress(sliceHex(payload, 0, 20));
    const account = getAddress(sliceHex(payload, 20, 40));
    const tokenId = Number(BigInt(sliceHex(payload, 40, 72)));
    return [erc721, account, tokenId];
  }

  private depositErc721(
    account: Address,
    erc721: Address,
    tokenId: number,
  ): string {
    const balance = this.getOrCreateBalance(account);
    balance.addErc721Token(erc721, tokenId);
    const noticePayload = {
      type: "erc721deposit",
      content: {
        address: account,
        erc721: erc721,
        tokenId: tokenId.toString(),
      },
    };
    return JSON.stringify(noticePayload);
  }

  withdrawErc721(
    application: Address,
    account: Address,
    erc721: Address,
    tokenId: number,
  ): Voucher {
    const balance = this.getOrCreateBalance(account);
    balance.removeErc721Token(erc721, tokenId);
    const call = encodeFunctionData({
      abi: erc721Abi,
      functionName: "safeTransferFrom",
      args: [application, account, BigInt(tokenId)],
    });
    console.log("Voucher creation success", {
      destination: erc721,
      payload: call,
    });

    return {
      destination: erc721,
      value: 0n,
      payload: call,
    };
  }

  transferErc721(
    from: Address,
    to: Address,
    erc721: Address,
    tokenId: number,
  ): string {
    const balanceFrom = this.getOrCreateBalance(from);
    const balanceTo = this.getOrCreateBalance(to);
    balanceFrom.removeErc721Token(erc721, tokenId);
    balanceTo.addErc721Token(erc721, tokenId);
    const noticePayload = {
      type: "erc721transfer",
      content: {
        from: from,
        to: to,
        erc721: erc721,
        tokenId: tokenId.toString(),
      },
    };
    console.info(
      `Token ERC-721 ${erc721} id:${tokenId} transferred from ${from} to ${to}`,
    );
    return JSON.stringify(noticePayload);
  }
}
```

### Voucher creation

The `withdrawErc721` method encodes `safeTransferFrom(application, recipient, tokenId)` and returns a voucher. NFTs deposited through the portal are held by your on-chain `Application` contract; pass `request.appContract` from the advance request as the `from` address. The voucher's `value` is `0n` because no Ether is sent with the call. See [withdrawing tokens](../development/asset-handling.md#withdrawing-tokens).

## Using the wallet

Now, let's create a simple application at the entry point `src/index.ts` to test the wallet’s functionality.

The [`Erc721Portal`](../api-reference/contracts/portals/Erc721Portal.md) contract moves ERC-721 tokens from the base layer into your application. Deposits arrive as advance requests whose `msgSender` is the portal address.

:::note Erc721Portal address
Run [`cartesi address-book`](../development/send-inputs-and-assets.md) and copy the `Erc721Portal` address for your network into `index.ts`. For a given rollups-contracts release, each portal has the same address on every supported network and on the devnet, but the address changes between releases: take it from `cartesi address-book` rather than from an older sample.
:::

```typescript
import {
  type AdvanceRequest,
  type InspectRequest,
  Rollup,
} from "@cartesi/rollup";
import {
  type Address,
  bytesToHex,
  getAddress,
  isAddressEqual,
  stringToHex,
} from "viem";
import { Wallet } from "./wallet/wallet";

// Replace with the Erc721Portal address from `cartesi address-book`
const ERC721_PORTAL: Address = "0xYOUR_ERC721_PORTAL_ADDRESS";

const rollup = new Rollup();
const wallet = new Wallet();

const handleAdvance = (request: AdvanceRequest): boolean => {
  console.log(
    `Received advance request from ${request.msgSender} with index ${request.index}`,
  );

  if (isAddressEqual(request.msgSender, ERC721_PORTAL)) {
    // Deposit: the portal names the collection, the depositor and the token ID
    const deposit = wallet.processErc721Deposit(bytesToHex(request.payload));
    rollup.emitNotice(stringToHex(deposit));
    return true;
  }

  // Transfer or withdrawal: always on behalf of the account that sent the input
  const owner = getAddress(request.msgSender);
  try {
    const { operation, erc721, to, tokenId } = JSON.parse(
      request.payload.toString("utf8"),
    );

    if (operation === "transfer") {
      const transfer = wallet.transferErc721(
        owner,
        getAddress(to),
        getAddress(erc721),
        Number(tokenId),
      );
      rollup.emitNotice(stringToHex(transfer));
    } else if (operation === "withdraw") {
      // The application contract holds the deposited NFTs, so it is the
      // `from` address of the `safeTransferFrom` call in the voucher
      const voucher = wallet.withdrawErc721(
        request.appContract,
        owner,
        getAddress(erc721),
        Number(tokenId),
      );
      rollup.emitVoucher(voucher);
    } else {
      throw new Error(`Unknown operation: ${operation}`);
    }
    return true;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("Error processing payload:", error);
    rollup.emitReport(stringToHex(`Error processing payload: ${error}`));
    return false;
  }
};

const handleInspect = (request: InspectRequest): void => {
  try {
    const [address, erc721] = request.payload.toString("utf8").split("/");
    if (address === undefined || erc721 === undefined) {
      throw new Error("expected userAddress/erc721TokenAddress");
    }
    const balance = wallet.getErc721Balance(
      getAddress(address),
      getAddress(erc721),
    );
    rollup.emitReport(stringToHex(JSON.stringify(balance)));
  } catch (error) {
    rollup.emitReport(
      stringToHex(`Error processing inspect payload: ${error}`),
    );
  }
};

await rollup.run({ advance: handleAdvance, inspect: handleInspect });
```

This code uses the `Rollup` class of [`@cartesi/rollup`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@cartesi/rollup/v/1.0.0-alpha.3), which the template already depends on: `rollup.run()` passes each request to `handleAdvance` or `handleInspect`, with the payload as a Node.js `Buffer`, and an advance handler rejects the input when it returns `false`.

Here is a breakdown of the wallet functionality:

- We handle deposits when the sender is the `Erc721Portal`. The portal writes the collection, the depositor's address and the token ID in the payload, and the wallet credits the token to the depositor.

- We parse the payload for other senders to determine the operation (`transfer` or `withdraw`).

- The account that sends the input is the owner of the operation: transfers and withdrawals always move tokens of `request.msgSender`, and the payload has no `from` field. Anyone can write any address in a JSON payload, but nobody can send an input on behalf of another account, so reading the owner from the payload would let anyone take anyone's NFTs.

- For `transfers`, we call `wallet.transferErc721` and create a notice with the parsed parameters.

- For `withdrawals`, we call `wallet.withdrawErc721` with the on-chain application address (`request.appContract`) as the `safeTransferFrom` sender, then emit a voucher to the token contract with `rollup.emitVoucher`.

- When an operation fails, for example because the sender does not own the token, we emit the error as a report with `rollup.emitReport` and reject the input. Inspect requests answer balance checks with a report as well.

## Build and run the application

With Docker running, [build your backend application](../development/running-an-application.md) by running:

```shell
cartesi build
```

To run your application, enter the command:

```shell
cartesi run
```

### Deposits

:::caution token approvals
An approval step is needed for the [**ERC721 token standard**](https://ethereum.org/en/developers/docs/standards/tokens/). This ensures you grant explicit permission for `Erc721Portal` to transfer tokens on your behalf.

Without this approval, the `Erc721Portal` cannot deposit your tokens to the Cartesi backend.

If you don't approve the `Erc721Portal` address before depositing, the call to `depositErc721Token` reverts with the token contract's insufficient-approval error (for example, `ERC721InsufficientApproval` in OpenZeppelin 5 tokens).
:::

To deposit ERC721 tokens interactively:

```bash
cartesi deposit erc721
```

The depositing account must own the token. `TestNFT` has a public `mint` function, so mint the token first as shown below.

Non-interactive alternative. Run from your **project root** (with `cartesi run` up). Resolve addresses from [`cartesi address-book`](../development/send-inputs-and-assets.md):

```bash
NFT=$(cartesi address-book TestNFT)
ERC721_PORTAL=$(cartesi address-book Erc721Portal)

cast send "$NFT" \
  "mint(address,uint256)" \
  0x23618e81E3f5cdF7f54C3d65f7FBc0aBf5B21E8f \
  1 \
  --rpc-url http://127.0.0.1:6751/anvil \
  --private-key 0xdbda1821b80551c9d65939329250298aa3472ba22feea921c0cf5d620ea67b97

cast send "$NFT" \
  "setApprovalForAll(address,bool)" \
  "$ERC721_PORTAL" \
  true \
  --rpc-url http://127.0.0.1:6751/anvil \
  --private-key 0xdbda1821b80551c9d65939329250298aa3472ba22feea921c0cf5d620ea67b97

cartesi deposit erc721 1 \
  --token "$NFT" \
  --project-name erc-721-token-wallet \
  --rpc-url http://127.0.0.1:6751/anvil
```

Skip the `mint` call if token ID `1` already exists; each token ID can be minted only once. On success, the CLI prints `✔ Approved 1 NFT` and `✔ Deposited 1 NFT to <application address>`.

### Balance checks (used in Inspect requests)

Inspect payloads use the form `userAddress/erc721TokenAddress` as a UTF-8 string. The node passes the request body to your application unchanged as the inspect payload, so send that string as the body. Example for user `0x23618e81E3f5cdF7f54C3d65f7FBc0aBf5B21E8f` and the `TestNFT` collection `0x0761b8e3aB06F458632974393C48765E6Ddc61bB`:

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:6751/inspect/erc-721-token-wallet \
  -H "Content-Type: text/plain" \
  -d '0x23618e81E3f5cdF7f54C3d65f7FBc0aBf5B21E8f/0x0761b8e3aB06F458632974393C48765E6Ddc61bB'
```

Replace the inspect path if your project name is not `erc-721-token-wallet` (see the URL printed by `cartesi run`). Replace the addresses in the body if you use different ones.

### Transfers and Withdrawals

To process transfers and withdrawals interactively, run the command below, select `String encoding`, then enter one of the sample payloads:

```bash
cartesi send
```

Non-interactive alternative (from your project root):

```bash
cartesi send --encoding string \
  '{"operation":"withdraw","erc721":"0x0761b8e3aB06F458632974393C48765E6Ddc61bB","tokenId":"1"}' \
  --project-name erc-721-token-wallet \
  --rpc-url http://127.0.0.1:6751/anvil
```

1. For transfers:

   ```js
   {"operation":"transfer","erc721":"0xTokenAddress","to":"0xToAddress","tokenId":"1"}
   ```

2. For withdrawals:

   ```js
   {"operation":"withdraw","erc721":"0xTokenAddress","tokenId":"1"}
   ```

Replace `0xTokenAddress` with the collection address (`TestNFT` in the samples above, `0x0761b8e3aB06F458632974393C48765E6Ddc61bB`). The wallet moves tokens of the account that sends the input: `cartesi send` sends from devnet account 8 (`0x23618e81E3f5cdF7f54C3d65f7FBc0aBf5B21E8f`), the account that made the deposit above. If you pass `--from` to send from another account, the application rejects the input with a report unless that account owns the token in the wallet.

### Using the explorer

[CartesiScan](https://cartesiscan.io/) is a web application that offers a comprehensive overview of your application. It provides expandable data regarding notices, vouchers, and reports.

Start the node with the explorer service enabled:

```shell
cartesi run --services explorer
```

The local explorer is then available at `http://localhost:6751/explorer` (same port as the application node—see [running an application](../development/running-an-application.md)). The explorer is not started by plain `cartesi run`; you must pass `--services explorer`.

You can execute your vouchers via the explorer to complete the withdrawal. A voucher becomes executable only after [its epoch](../api-reference/backend/vouchers.md#epoch-configuration) closes and the epoch's claim is accepted on-chain; until then, execution reverts.

   You can access the complete project implementation [here](https://github.com/Mugen-Builders/docs_examples/tree/af7e52df98999a28223283814bfde9a4f6f1add3/erc-721-token-wallet)!

---
id: ether-wallet
title: Integrating Ether wallet functionality
---

This tutorial will build a basic Ether wallet inside a Cartesi backend application using TypeScript.

The goal is to have a backend application to track balances and receive, transfer, and withdraw Ether.

## Setting up the project

First, create a new TypeScript project using the [Cartesi CLI](../development/installation.md#cartesi-cli) and move into its directory:

```bash
cartesi create ether-wallet --template typescript
cd ether-wallet
```

The template manages its packages with [pnpm](https://pnpm.io), through [corepack](https://nodejs.org/api/corepack.html). If the `pnpm` command is not available, enable it with:

```bash
corepack enable pnpm
```

Now, install [`viem`](https://viem.sh/) as a development dependency:

```bash
pnpm add -D viem@2.57.19
```

Then replace the contents of `rolldown.config.ts` with the following, so that rolldown bundles viem into your application and only leaves out the `@cartesi/rollup` native addon:

```typescript
import { defineConfig } from "rolldown";

export default defineConfig({
  input: "src/index.ts",
  platform: "node",
  // only the @cartesi/rollup native addon stays out of the bundle: viem and
  // any other pure JavaScript dependency are bundled into dist/index.mjs
  external: ["@cartesi/rollup"],
  output: {
    file: "dist/index.mjs",
    format: "esm",
  },
});
```

`cartesi build` installs the packages listed under `dependencies` inside an emulated RISC-V container, where pnpm can crash with a segmentation fault while it installs viem. A bundled development dependency is not installed there. See [adding dependencies](../development/creating-an-application.md#adding-dependencies-in-javascript-and-typescript).

## Building the Ether wallet

Our wallet will have two main classes: `Balance` and `Wallet`. Let's implement each of these:

Create a file named `balance.ts` in the `src/wallet` directory and add the following code:

```typescript
import type { Address } from "viem";

export class Balance {
  constructor(
    private readonly address: Address,
    private ether: bigint = 0n,
  ) {}

  getEther(): bigint {
    return this.ether;
  }

  increaseEther(amount: bigint): void {
    if (amount < 0n) {
      throw new Error(`Invalid amount: ${amount}`);
    }
    this.ether += amount;
  }

  decreaseEther(amount: bigint): void {
    if (amount < 0n) {
      throw new Error(`Invalid amount: ${amount}`);
    }
    if (this.ether < amount) {
      throw new Error(`Insufficient balance for ${this.address}`);
    }
    this.ether -= amount;
  }
}
```

The `Balance` class represents an individual account's balance. It includes methods for getting, increasing, and decreasing the Ether balance.

Now, create a file named `wallet.ts` in the `src/wallet` directory and add the following code:

```typescript
import type { Voucher } from "@cartesi/rollup";
import { type Address, getAddress, type Hex, sliceHex } from "viem";
import { Balance } from "./balance";

export class Wallet {
  private accounts: Map<Address, Balance> = new Map();

  private getOrCreateBalance(address: Address): Balance {
    const key = getAddress(address);
    let balance = this.accounts.get(key);
    if (!balance) {
      balance = new Balance(key);
      this.accounts.set(key, balance);
    }
    return balance;
  }

  getBalance(address: Address): bigint {
    return this.getOrCreateBalance(address).getEther();
  }

  depositEther(payload: Hex): string {
    const [address, amount] = this.parseDepositPayload(payload);
    const balance = this.getOrCreateBalance(address);
    balance.increaseEther(amount);
    console.log(
      `After deposit, balance for ${address} is ${balance.getEther()}`,
    );
    return JSON.stringify({
      type: "etherDeposit",
      address,
      amount: amount.toString(),
    });
  }

  withdrawEther(address: Address, amount: bigint): Voucher {
    const balance = this.getOrCreateBalance(address);
    balance.decreaseEther(amount);
    console.log(
      `After withdrawal, balance for ${address} is ${balance.getEther()}`,
    );
    return this.encodeWithdrawCall(address, amount);
  }

  transferEther(from: Address, to: Address, amount: bigint): string {
    const fromBalance = this.getOrCreateBalance(from);
    const toBalance = this.getOrCreateBalance(to);
    fromBalance.decreaseEther(amount);
    toBalance.increaseEther(amount);
    console.log(
      `After transfer, balance for ${from} is ${fromBalance.getEther()}`,
    );
    console.log(`After transfer, balance for ${to} is ${toBalance.getEther()}`);
    return JSON.stringify({
      type: "etherTransfer",
      from,
      to,
      amount: amount.toString(),
    });
  }

  private parseDepositPayload(payload: Hex): [Address, bigint] {
    const addressData = sliceHex(payload, 0, 20);
    const amountData = sliceHex(payload, 20, 52);
    return [getAddress(addressData), BigInt(amountData)];
  }

  private encodeWithdrawCall(receiver: Address, amount: bigint): Voucher {
    return {
      destination: receiver,
      value: amount,
      payload: "0x",
    };
  }
}
```

The `Wallet` class manages multiple accounts and provides methods for everyday wallet operations. Key features include storing balances, centralizing the logic for retrieving or creating a balance, and depositing, withdrawing, and transferring Ether.

`parseDepositPayload` and `encodeWithdrawCall` handle the low-level details of working with the base layer data.

### Voucher creation

The `encodeWithdrawCall` method returns a voucher, typed with the `Voucher` interface of `@cartesi/rollup`. Creating vouchers is a crucial concept in Cartesi Rollups for executing withdrawal operations on the base layer chain.

In Rollups v2, the on-chain [`Application`](../api-reference/contracts/application.md) contract executes vouchers through [`executeOutput()`](../api-reference/contracts/application.md#executeoutput), which decodes a voucher as `(destination, value, payload)` and performs a [`safeCall`](https://github.com/cartesi/rollups-contracts/blob/v3.0.0-alpha.10/src/library/LibAddress.sol) to `destination` with the specified wei `value`. Ether held by your application (`request.appContract` on each advance request) is sent to the recipient this way.

For a plain Ether transfer, leave `payload` empty (`0x`, no calldata). The voucher fields are:

- `destination`: The address that receives the withdrawn Ether.
- `value`: The withdrawal amount in wei, as a `bigint`. `@cartesi/rollup` encodes it as the voucher's 32-byte `uint256`.
- `payload`: `0x` when you are not calling a function on the recipient. A non-empty payload, even 32 zero bytes such as `zeroHash`, makes the voucher revert with `TargetHasNoCode` when the recipient is a wallet with no code (see [asset handling](../development/asset-handling.md#withdrawing-ether)).

## Using the Ether wallet

Now, let's create a simple application at the entry point, `src/index.ts`, to test the wallet functionality.

The [`EtherPortal`](../api-reference/contracts/portals/EtherPortal.md) contract allows anyone to transfer Ether into your application. All deposits are made via the `EtherPortal` contract.

:::note EtherPortal address
Run [`cartesi address-book`](../development/send-inputs-and-assets.md) and copy the `EtherPortal` address for your network into `index.ts`. For a given rollups-contracts release, each portal has the same address on every supported network and on the devnet, but the address changes between releases: take it from `cartesi address-book` rather than from an older sample.
:::

```typescript
import {
  type AdvanceRequest,
  type InspectRequest,
  Rollup,
} from "@cartesi/rollup";
import {
  type Address,
  bytesToHex,
  getAddress,
  isAddressEqual,
  stringToHex,
} from "viem";
import { Wallet } from "./wallet/wallet";

// Replace with the EtherPortal address from `cartesi address-book`
const ETHER_PORTAL: Address = "0xYOUR_ETHER_PORTAL_ADDRESS";

const rollup = new Rollup();
const wallet = new Wallet();

const handleAdvance = (request: AdvanceRequest): boolean => {
  console.log(
    `Received advance request from ${request.msgSender} with index ${request.index}`,
  );

  if (isAddressEqual(request.msgSender, ETHER_PORTAL)) {
    // Deposit: the portal names the depositor in the payload
    const deposit = wallet.depositEther(bytesToHex(request.payload));
    rollup.emitNotice(stringToHex(deposit));
    return true;
  }

  // Transfer or withdrawal: always on behalf of the account that sent the input
  const owner = getAddress(request.msgSender);
  try {
    const { operation, to, amount } = JSON.parse(
      request.payload.toString("utf8"),
    );

    if (operation === "transfer") {
      const transfer = wallet.transferEther(owner, getAddress(to), BigInt(amount));
      rollup.emitNotice(stringToHex(transfer));
    } else if (operation === "withdraw") {
      // The application contract (request.appContract) holds the deposited
      // Ether and sends it to the owner when the voucher is executed
      const voucher = wallet.withdrawEther(owner, BigInt(amount));
      rollup.emitVoucher(voucher);
    } else {
      throw new Error(`Unknown operation: ${operation}`);
    }
    return true;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("Error processing payload:", error);
    rollup.emitReport(stringToHex(`Error processing payload: ${error}`));
    return false;
  }
};

const handleInspect = (request: InspectRequest): void => {
  try {
    const address = getAddress(request.payload.toString("utf8"));
    const balance = wallet.getBalance(address);
    rollup.emitReport(stringToHex(`Balance for ${address} is ${balance} wei`));
  } catch (error) {
    rollup.emitReport(
      stringToHex(`Error processing inspect payload: ${error}`),
    );
  }
};

await rollup.run({ advance: handleAdvance, inspect: handleInspect });
```

This code uses the `Rollup` class of [`@cartesi/rollup`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@cartesi/rollup/v/1.0.0-alpha.3), which the template already depends on and which talks directly to the Cartesi Machine. `rollup.run()` waits for each request and passes it to `handleAdvance` or `handleInspect`, with the request payload as a Node.js `Buffer`. An advance handler accepts the input when it returns `true` and rejects it when it returns `false`: the node then discards the notices and vouchers of that input and reverts the application state, but keeps its reports.

Here is a breakdown of the wallet functionality:

- `handleAdvance` handles Ether deposits (from `EtherPortal`) and user operations (transfers/withdrawals).

- We handle deposits and create a notice when the sender is the `EtherPortal`. The portal writes the depositor's address and the amount in the payload, and the wallet credits that address.

- We parse the payload for other senders to determine the operation (`transfer` or `withdraw`).

- The account that sends the input is the owner of the operation: transfers and withdrawals always debit `request.msgSender`, and the payload has no `from` field. Anyone can write any address in a JSON payload, but nobody can send an input on behalf of another account, so reading the owner from the payload would let anyone move anyone's balance.

- For `transfers`, we call `wallet.transferEther` and create a notice with the parsed parameters.

- For withdrawals, we call `wallet.withdrawEther` and emit a voucher with `rollup.emitVoucher`. When it is executed, the voucher sends wei from the on-chain Application (`request.appContract`) to the owner.

- When an operation fails, for example because of an insufficient balance or an unknown operation, we emit the error as a report with `rollup.emitReport` and reject the input. Inspect requests answer balance checks with a report as well.

## Build and run the application

With Docker running, [build your backend application](../development/running-an-application.md) by running:

### Deposits

### Balance checks (used in Inspect requests)


The node passes the request body to your application unchanged as the inspect payload, so the body is the address to query as plain text (here `0x23618e81E3f5cdF7f54C3d65f7FBc0aBf5B21E8f`). Replace the inspect path if your project name is not `ether-wallet` (see the URL printed by `cartesi run`).

### Transfer and Withdrawals

Transfers and withdrawal requests will be sent as generic json strings that will be parsed and processed.

To process transfers and withdrawals interactively, run the command below, select `String encoding`, then follow the prompts:

```bash

```

```bash
cartesi send --encoding string \

  --project-name ether-wallet \
  --rpc-url http://127.0.0.1:6751/anvil
```

Here are the sample payloads as one-liners, ready to be used in your code:

1. For transfers:

   ```js
   {"operation":"transfer","to":"0x3f2bd12ea0b8604c2af5bf241f6a606e892a403a","amount":"1000000000000000000"}
   ```

2. For withdrawals:

   ```js

   ```

The wallet debits the account that sends the input: `cartesi send` sends from devnet account 8 (`0x23618e81E3f5cdF7f54C3d65f7FBc0aBf5B21E8f`), the account that made the deposit above. Pass `--from` to send from another account; the application then debits that account, and rejects the input with a report such as `Error processing payload: Error: Insufficient balance for 0xa0Ee7A142d267C1f36714E4a8F75612F20a79720` when it has no balance in the wallet.

### Using the explorer

You can execute your vouchers via the explorer to complete the withdrawal. A voucher becomes executable only after [its epoch](../api-reference/backend/vouchers.md#epoch-configuration) closes and the epoch's claim is accepted on-chain; until then, execution reverts.

    title: Source code for the Marketplace Application

In this tutorial we'll be building a simple NFT Marketplace application, where users are able to deposit a unique token to be sold at a fixed price, then other users are able to purchase and withdraw these purchased tokens to their wallet.

This Tutorial is built using an Object oriented approach and aims to cover, application creation, Notice, Voucher and Report generation, we'll also be decoding and consuming the payload passed alongside advance and inspect requests.

## How the Marketplace Works

Before setting up the project, here is how the marketplace application works.
This tutorial uses an Object-Oriented approach. This means we will create a main Marketplace object that stores the application state and provides methods to update or retrieve that state. Then we'll build other handler functions that utilizes other helper functions to decode user requests then call the appropriate method to update the marketplace object.

For simplicity, our marketplace will support only:

- One specific ERC-721 (NFT) contract: This is the only collection users can list.

- One specific ERC-20 token: This is the token users will use to purchase NFTs.

### Advance Requests

**1. Depositing / Listing NFTs**

- A user sends an NFT to the Cartesi application through the ERC-721 Portal.
- When the application receives the deposit payload, it automatically lists the NFT for sale at a fixed price.
- The price is the same for every NFT in this tutorial to keep things simple.

**2. Depositing Payment Tokens**

- Users can then send the marketplace’s payment token to the application through the ERC-20 Portal.
- The application keeps track of how many tokens each user has deposited.

**3. Buying an NFT**

- When a user decides to buy an NFT listed on the marketplace, the application checks:
  - Is the NFT still listed?
  - Does the user have enough deposited tokens?

- If the transaction is valid, the marketplace transfers the payment token to the seller then creates a voucher that sends the purchased NFT to the buyer.

- If a check fails, the application emits a report with the reason and rejects the input.

### Inspect Requests

The Inspect route will support three simple read-only queries:

**1. `get_user_erc20_balance`**

**Description:** Shows how many tokens a user has stored in the marketplace.

**Input:** User's address

**Output:** Amount of ERC-20 tokens deposited.

**2. `get_token_owner`**

**Description:** Returns the current owner of a specific NFT.

**Input:** Token ID

**Output:** Address of current token owner. After a purchase the owner is the zero address: the NFT leaves the marketplace with the voucher.

**3. `get_all_listed_tokens`**

**Description:** Shows all NFTs currently listed for sale.

**Input:** (none)

**Output:** Array of Token IDs currently listed for sale.

The build is faster, but it depends on that third-party index.

## Build and Run your Application

Once you have your application logic written out, the next step is to build the application, this is done by running the below commands using the Cartesi CLI:

```shell
cartesi build
```

- Expected Logs:
  

The build command compiles your application then builds a Cartesi machine that contains your application.

Next, start the newly built machine, along with the other services it needs (an Anvil network, the inspect service and so on), by running:

```bash
cartesi run
```

If the `run` command is successful, you should see logs similar to this:


## Interacting with your Marketplace Application

Once your Marketplace application is up and running (via cartesi run), you can interact with it in two main ways — either by sending on-chain transactions through the local Anvil network (Advance requests) or by making HTTP requests directly to the node's inspect endpoint (Inspect requests).

In this section, we’ll focus on using the Cartesi CLI to send Advance requests, since it provides a much simpler and faster way to test your application locally.

:::note Inspect endpoint
If your application is running on a different port or has a different name from marketplace, remember to replace the inspect endpoint http://127.0.0.1:6751/inspect/marketplace with the one displayed after running the cartesi run command.
Also, ensure that all CLI commands are executed from the root directory of your application.
:::

### 1. Mint an ERC-721 Token and Grant Approval

With your Marketplace application now deployed, the first step is to mint the NFT you plan to list and grant approval for it to be transferred via the ERC-721 portal.
Since our app uses the test ERC-721 and ERC-20 contracts automatically deployed by the CLI, you can use the commands below to mint your token and set the necessary approvals. The commands use the `TestNFT` and `Erc721Portal` addresses printed by `cartesi address-book`, the same addresses hard-coded in the application code.

- Mint token ID 1:
  
```bash
cast send 0x0761b8e3aB06F458632974393C48765E6Ddc61bB \
  "mint(address,uint256)" \
  0x23618e81E3f5cdF7f54C3d65f7FBc0aBf5B21E8f 1 \
  --rpc-url http://127.0.0.1:6751/anvil \
  --private-key 0xdbda1821b80551c9d65939329250298aa3472ba22feea921c0cf5d620ea67b97
```

This command calls the public `mint` function in the `TestNFT` contract deployed by the CLI, minting token `ID 1` to the address `0x23618e81E3f5cdF7f54C3d65f7FBc0aBf5B21E8f`.

- Grant approval to the ERC721-Portal:

Before an NFT can be deposited into the application, the portal contract must have permission to transfer it on behalf of the owner. Use the following command to grant that approval:

```bash
cast send 0x0761b8e3aB06F458632974393C48765E6Ddc61bB \
  "setApprovalForAll(address,bool)" \
  0x397c352d18DFf47CC8a6143403142cf7afd5Ff7E true \
  --rpc-url http://127.0.0.1:6751/anvil \
  --private-key 0xdbda1821b80551c9d65939329250298aa3472ba22feea921c0cf5d620ea67b97
```

### 2. Deposit NFT with ID 1 to the Marketplace [advance request]

Now that the NFT is minted and approved, it’s time to list it on the marketplace.
We’ll do this by depositing it using the Cartesi CLI:

```bash
cartesi deposit erc721
```

The CLI will prompt you for the token ID (enter 1) and the token address (press Enter to use the default test token).
Under the hood, the CLI approves the portal for the token and calls `depositErc721Token`; the portal transfers the NFT from your address to the application contract and adds an input with the deposit details.

Once the deposit succeeds, the terminal running your application should show logs similar to the following. The sample logs on this page come from the Rust implementation, which runs the rollup HTTP server; the other languages print their own messages:

```bash
[INFO  rollup_http_server::http_service] received new request of type ADVANCE
[INFO  actix_web::middleware::logger] 127.0.0.1 "POST /finish HTTP/1.1" 200 750 "-" "-" 0.020416
Received finish status 200 OK
Received advance request data {"request_type":"advance_state","data":{"metadata":{"chain_id":31337,"app_contract":"0x1173736abe1b9fd5af86604089c8264826c94fcd","msg_sender":"0x397c352d18dff47cc8a6143403142cf7afd5ff7e","block_number":38,"block_timestamp":1794920122,"prev_randao":"0xed9592734017a764b86b7e50541f4db382e676771985cce5ab423a7afb0aa486","input_index":0},"payload":""}}
Deposited and listed token: 0x0761b8e3ab06f458632974393c48765e6ddc61bb, Receiver: 0x23618e81e3f5cdf7f54c3d65f7fbc0abf5b21e8f, Token ID: 1
Token deposit and listing processed successfully
[INFO  actix_web::middleware::logger] 127.0.0.1 "POST /notice HTTP/1.1" 201 11 "-" "-" 0.001088
Notice generation successful
Sending finish
```

### 3. View All NFTs Listed on the Marketplace [inspect request]

After depositing, your NFT is automatically listed.
To verify this, you can query the marketplace for all listed tokens using an Inspect request:

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:6751/inspect/marketplace \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"method":"get_all_listed_tokens"}'
```

This call returns a hex payload containing a list of all listed tokens on the marketplace.

```bash
{"status":"Accepted","reports":[{"payload":"0x416c6c206c697374656420746f6b656e73206172653a2031"}],"processed_input_count":1}
```

The payload hex `0x416c6...3a2031` when decoded, returns `All listed tokens are: 1`. Thereby confirming that the token with `Id 1` has successfully been listed.

### 4. Deposit ERC20 token for making purchases [advance request]

With the NFT successfully listed for sale, it's time to attempt to purchase this token, but before we do that, we first need to deposit enough tokens to purchase the listed NFT. Since our marketplace lists all NFTs at the price of `100` `TestToken` tokens (FUN), we'll be minting 100 tokens to the new address we'll be using to purchase, before proceeding with the purchase. `TestToken` starts with no balance on a new devnet, and its `mint` function is public.

- Mint the required tokens to the purchase address.
  
```bash
cast send 0x86EA17052C8e335Ad830B54EF566274EAB46B852 \
"mint(address,uint256)" 0x70997970C51812dc3A010C7d01b50e0d17dc79C8 100000000000000000000 \
--private-key 0xdbda1821b80551c9d65939329250298aa3472ba22feea921c0cf5d620ea67b97 \
--rpc-url http://127.0.0.1:6751/anvil
```

- Deposit 100 tokens to the marketplace application.

```bash
cartesi deposit erc20 --from 0x70997970C51812dc3A010C7d01b50e0d17dc79C8
```

The CLI will prompt you for the token address (press Enter to use the default test token), and then the amount of tokens we intend to deposit `(100)`. The CLI would finally proceed to grant the necessary approvals after which it would deposit the tokens to our application.

On a successful deposit our application should return logs that look like this:

```bash
[INFO  rollup_http_server::http_service] received new request of type ADVANCE
[INFO  actix_web::middleware::logger] 127.0.0.1 "POST /finish HTTP/1.1" 200 494 "-" "-" 0.019008
Received finish status 200 OK
Received advance request data {"request_type":"advance_state","data":{"metadata":{"chain_id":31337,"app_contract":"0x1173736abe1b9fd5af86604089c8264826c94fcd","msg_sender":"0x3332de61a8bb9ac84893b2f552fe81c9a6dc5419","block_number":81,"block_timestamp":1794920208,"prev_randao":"0x4b9d05d49847fa57352b6fa9b22496e7dd0c7a74bb8ce84534d7c9084d448a2d","input_index":1},"payload":"0x86ea17052c8e335ad830b54ef566274eab46b85270997970c51812dc3a010c7d01b50e0d17dc79c80000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000056bc75e2d63100000"}}
Deposited token: 0x86ea17052c8e335ad830b54ef566274eab46b852, Receiver: 0x70997970c51812dc3a010c7d01b50e0d17dc79c8, Amount: 100000000000000000000
Token deposit processed successfully
Sending finish
```

### 5. Purchase Token with ID 1 [advance request]

Now that the buyer has deposited funds, we can proceed to purchase the NFT. Use the following Cartesi CLI flow:

```bash
cartesi send --from 0x70997970C51812dc3A010C7d01b50e0d17dc79C8
✔ Input String encoding
✔ Input (as string) {"method": "purchase_token", "token_id": "1"}
✔ Input sent: 0x209f81a43a03ac57aa22a80ce87978c02fe7d02ec298714186f692af59af4cf9
```

This sends a purchase request for token ID `1` from the buyer address. Pass `token_id` as a string, as above: the application reads it as a string and rejects the purchase, with the report `Missing or invalid token_id field in payload`, when it is a number. The marketplace validates the request (token listed and sufficient balance), executes the purchase, and emits the voucher to transfer the NFT to the buyer.

```bash
[INFO  rollup_http_server::http_service] received new request of type ADVANCE
[INFO  actix_web::middleware::logger] 127.0.0.1 "POST /finish HTTP/1.1" 200 440 "-" "-" 0.002624
Received finish status 200 OK
Received advance request data {"request_type":"advance_state","data":{"metadata":{"chain_id":31337,"app_contract":"0x1173736abe1b9fd5af86604089c8264826c94fcd","msg_sender":"0x70997970c51812dc3a010c7d01b50e0d17dc79c8","block_number":88,"block_timestamp":1794920222,"prev_randao":"0x6566eb1f4a1fee4e613e0b3e112fdde41187675bbdf6c90dfbdfa3403763fa21","input_index":2},"payload":"0x7b226d6574686f64223a202270757263686173655f746f6b656e222c2022746f6b656e5f6964223a202231227d"}}
Token purchased successfully
[INFO  actix_web::middleware::logger] 127.0.0.1 "POST /voucher HTTP/1.1" 201 11 "-" "-" 0.016704
Voucher generation successful
Token purchased and Withdrawn successfully
Sending finish
```

### 6. Recheck NFTs Listed on the Marketplace [inspect request]

Finally, we can confirm that the purchased NFT has been removed from the listings by running the inspect query again:

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:6751/inspect/marketplace \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"method":"get_all_listed_tokens"}'
```

This call returns a hex payload like below:

```bash
{"status":"Accepted","reports":[{"payload":"0x416c6c206c697374656420746f6b656e73206172653a20"}],"processed_input_count":3}
```

The payload hex `0x416c6...653a20` when decoded, returns `All listed tokens are: ` (an empty list). Thereby verifying that the token with `Id 1` has successfully been sold and no longer listed for sale in the marketplace.

## Conclusion

Congratulations!!!

You’ve successfully built and interacted with your own Marketplace application on Cartesi. 

This example covered essential Cartesi concepts such as routing, asset management, voucher generation, and the use of both Inspect and Advance routes.

For a more detailed version of this code, you can check the `marketplace` folder for your selected language in [this repository](https://github.com/Mugen-Builders/Counter-X-Marketplace-apps/tree/3ea44735b2237366208f726e36a4660c55a41f1e)

# Building a React Frontend for Cartesi Apps

This guide builds a React frontend that talks to a Cartesi application with the Cartesi TypeScript packages, [wagmi](https://wagmi.sh) and [viem](https://viem.sh):

- `@cartesi/react` provides the `CartesiProvider` and the React hooks that read the node's JSON-RPC API (`useOutputs`, `useReports`, `useWaitForInput`, `useApplications`, and more). It was previously published as `@cartesi/wagmi`.
- `@cartesi/client` provides the node client, the contract ABIs and addresses (`@cartesi/client/abi`), and helpers such as `getInputsAdded` and `toOutputArgs`. It was previously published as `@cartesi/viem`.

Sending inputs, depositing assets and executing vouchers are plain contract calls: you make them with wagmi's `useWriteContract` and the ABIs and addresses exported by `@cartesi/client/abi`. The packages no longer ship `walletActionsL1` / `addInput` / `depositEther` helpers.

:::note
This guide has been tested with Cartesi CLI 2.0.0-alpha.42 (rollups-node v2.0.0-alpha.14, rollups-contracts v3.0.0-alpha.10), `@cartesi/react` 2.0.0-alpha.45 and `@cartesi/client` 2.0.0-alpha.41.

Both Cartesi packages are published under the `alpha` tag, and their `latest` tag points to `0.0.0`. Always install the exact versions shown below.
:::

## Prerequisites

- Node.js and pnpm.
- A Cartesi application running locally with the Cartesi CLI. Start it with a short epoch so that vouchers become executable within seconds (the default epoch is 720 blocks, about 24 minutes):

  ```bash
  cartesi build
  cartesi run --epoch-length 10
  ```

  `cartesi run` prints the local endpoints and the application address. With the default port (6751):

  | Service | URL |
  | --- | --- |
  | Local chain (anvil, chain id 31337) | `http://127.0.0.1:6751/anvil` |
  | Cartesi node JSON-RPC | `http://127.0.0.1:6751/rpc` |
  | Inspect | `http://127.0.0.1:6751/inspect/<app-name-or-address>` |

  The application address is the one in the line `<app-name> contract deployed at 0x...`.

## Installation

Bootstrap a React + TypeScript project with `create-wagmi`:

```bash
pnpm create wagmi@2.0.19 my-cartesi-webapp --template vite-react
cd my-cartesi-webapp
```

The template lists every dependency as `latest`. Install the Cartesi packages and pin all dependencies to the versions this guide was tested with:

```bash
pnpm add --save-exact react@19.3.1 react-dom@19.3.1 wagmi@3.7.11 viem@2.57.20 @tanstack/react-query@5.107.1 @cartesi/react@2.0.0-alpha.45 @cartesi/client@2.0.0-alpha.41
pnpm add --save-dev --save-exact typescript@7.0.2 vite@8.3.8 @vitejs/plugin-react@6.3.0 @types/react@19.3.0 @types/react-dom@19.3.0 @wagmi/cli@2.10.1
```

`@cartesi/client` is installed directly (and not only as a dependency of `@cartesi/react`) because the components import its ABIs and helpers.

## Project Structure

```plaintext
my-cartesi-webapp/
├── .env.local                  # Environment variables (project root, next to package.json)
└── src/
    ├── components/
    │   ├── CartesiApps.tsx     # To list all applications
    │   ├── CartesiInput.tsx    # To send inputs
    │   ├── CartesiInspect.tsx  # To inspect the application state
    │   ├── CartesiOutputs.tsx  # To read outputs and reports
    │   ├── CartesiStatus.tsx   # Application, epochs and inputs
    │   ├── DepositERC20.tsx    # To deposit ERC-20 tokens
    │   ├── DepositEther.tsx    # To deposit Ether
    │   ├── ExecuteVoucher.tsx  # To execute a voucher on the base layer
    │   └── InputTracker.tsx    # To wait for an input to be processed
    ├── providers/
    │   └── Web3Provider.tsx    # Wagmi, React Query and Cartesi providers
    ├── App.tsx                 # Main application component
    ├── main.tsx                # Entry point
    ├── vite-env.d.ts           # Types of the environment variables
    └── wagmi.ts                # Wagmi configuration file
```

## Core Components

### 1. Configure the local environment

Vite loads environment files from the project root, so create `.env.local` next to `package.json` (not inside `src/`). Replace the application address with the one printed by `cartesi run`, and change the port if you started the node with `--port`:

```bash title=".env.local"
VITE_ANVIL_RPC_URL=http://127.0.0.1:6751/anvil
VITE_CARTESI_RPC_URL=http://127.0.0.1:6751/rpc
VITE_CARTESI_INSPECT_URL=http://127.0.0.1:6751/inspect
VITE_CARTESI_APP_ADDRESS=<0x_your_app_address>
VITE_DEVNET_ACCOUNT=0xa0Ee7A142d267C1f36714E4a8F75612F20a79720
```

`VITE_DEVNET_ACCOUNT` is one of the accounts the devnet funds from the default `test test ... junk` mnemonic (index 9). Do not use the first account (index 0): the local node signs its claims with it.

Restart `pnpm dev` whenever you change `.env.local`. Declare the variables in `src/vite-env.d.ts` so that TypeScript knows them:

```ts title="src/vite-env.d.ts"
/// <reference types="vite/client" />

interface ImportMetaEnv {
  readonly VITE_ANVIL_RPC_URL: string
  readonly VITE_CARTESI_RPC_URL: string
  readonly VITE_CARTESI_INSPECT_URL: string
  readonly VITE_CARTESI_APP_ADDRESS: `0x${string}`
  readonly VITE_DEVNET_ACCOUNT: `0x${string}`
}
```

Replace `src/wagmi.ts` with a configuration for the local devnet (chain id 31337):

```ts title="src/wagmi.ts"
import { defineChain } from 'viem'
import { createConfig, http, injected, mock } from 'wagmi'

// The local chain started by `cartesi run`
export const cartesiDevnet = defineChain({
  id: 31337,
  name: 'Cartesi Devnet',
  nativeCurrency: { name: 'Ether', symbol: 'ETH', decimals: 18 },
  rpcUrls: { default: { http: [import.meta.env.VITE_ANVIL_RPC_URL] } },
  testnet: true,
})

export const config = createConfig({
  chains: [cartesiDevnet],
  connectors: [
    // Browser wallets such as MetaMask
    injected(),
    // Local devnet only: acts as VITE_DEVNET_ACCOUNT, which the devnet keeps
    // unlocked, so no browser wallet is needed. Remove it for real networks.
    mock({ accounts: [import.meta.env.VITE_DEVNET_ACCOUNT] }),
  ],
  transports: {
    [cartesiDevnet.id]: http(),
  },
})

declare module 'wagmi' {
  interface Register {
    config: typeof config
  }
}
```

:::note
To use MetaMask instead of the devnet connector, add a network with chain id `31337` and RPC URL `http://127.0.0.1:6751/anvil`, import the private key of a devnet account other than account 0, and connect with the **Injected** button.
:::

### 2. Setting up Providers

Create `src/providers/Web3Provider.tsx`. `CartesiProvider` creates the Cartesi node client that every Cartesi hook uses, and it must be inside the `QueryClientProvider`:

```tsx title="src/providers/Web3Provider.tsx"
import type { ReactNode } from 'react'
import { CartesiProvider } from '@cartesi/react'
import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import { WagmiProvider } from 'wagmi'
import { config } from '../wagmi'

const queryClient = new QueryClient()

export function Web3Provider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <WagmiProvider config={config}>
      <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
        <CartesiProvider rpcUrl={import.meta.env.VITE_CARTESI_RPC_URL}>
          {children}
        </CartesiProvider>
      </QueryClientProvider>
    </WagmiProvider>
  )
}
```

Replace `src/main.tsx` so that the whole app is wrapped by `Web3Provider` (the template's own `WagmiProvider` and `QueryClientProvider` move into it):

```tsx title="src/main.tsx"
import React from 'react'
import ReactDOM from 'react-dom/client'

import App from './App.tsx'
import { Web3Provider } from './providers/Web3Provider.tsx'

import './index.css'

ReactDOM.createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(
  <React.StrictMode>
    <Web3Provider>
      <App />
    </Web3Provider>
  </React.StrictMode>,
)
```

### 3. Sending Inputs to Cartesi Application

The `InputBox` contract receives arbitrary blobs (called "inputs") from anyone and is deployed at the same address on all supported chains. Call its `addInput` function with wagmi's `useWriteContract`, using the ABI and address exported by `@cartesi/client/abi`. The `InputAdded` event of the transaction carries the index of the new input, which `getInputsAdded` extracts from the receipt.

Create `src/components/InputTracker.tsx`. `useWaitForInput` polls the node until the input is processed and returns it with its status (`ACCEPTED`, `REJECTED`, `EXCEPTION`, ...). Input indexes are `bigint`s:

```tsx title="src/components/InputTracker.tsx"
import { useWaitForInput } from '@cartesi/react'
import type { Address } from 'viem'

interface InputTrackerProps {
  applicationAddress: Address
  inputIndex: bigint
}

export function InputTracker({ applicationAddress, inputIndex }: InputTrackerProps) {
  const { data: input, isLoading, error } = useWaitForInput({
    application: applicationAddress,
    inputIndex,
  })

  if (error) return <p>Failed to wait for input #{inputIndex.toString()}: {error.message}</p>
  if (isLoading) return <p>Waiting for input #{inputIndex.toString()} to be processed...</p>

  return (
    <p>
      Input #{inputIndex.toString()} processed with status: <strong>{input?.status}</strong>
    </p>
  )
}
```

Create `src/components/CartesiInput.tsx`:

```tsx title="src/components/CartesiInput.tsx"
import { useState } from 'react'
import { stringToHex, type Address } from 'viem'
import { useConnection, useWaitForTransactionReceipt, useWriteContract } from 'wagmi'
import { getInputsAdded } from '@cartesi/client'
import { inputBoxAbi, inputBoxAddress } from '@cartesi/client/abi'
import { InputTracker } from './InputTracker'

interface CartesiInputProps {
  applicationAddress: Address
}

export function CartesiInput({ applicationAddress }: CartesiInputProps) {
  const [input, setInput] = useState('')
  const { address } = useConnection()
  const { mutate: writeContract, data: hash, isPending, error } = useWriteContract()
  const { data: receipt, isLoading: isConfirming } = useWaitForTransactionReceipt({ hash })

  // index of the input added by the transaction
  const inputIndex = receipt ? getInputsAdded(receipt)[0]?.index : undefined

  const sendInput = () => {
    writeContract(
      {
        address: inputBoxAddress,
        abi: inputBoxAbi,
        functionName: 'addInput',
        args: [applicationAddress, stringToHex(input)],
      },
      { onSuccess: () => setInput('') },
    )
  }

  return (
    <div>
      <h3>Send Input</h3>
      <textarea
        value={input}
        onChange={(e) => setInput(e.target.value)}
        placeholder="Enter your input message..."
        rows={4}
        disabled={isPending}
      />
      <button onClick={sendInput} disabled={!address || isPending || !input.trim()}>
        {isPending ? 'Sending...' : 'Send Input'}
      </button>

      {error && <p>Failed to send input: {error.message}</p>}
      {hash && <p>Transaction: <code>{hash}</code>{isConfirming && ' (confirming...)'}</p>}
      {inputIndex !== undefined && (
        <InputTracker applicationAddress={applicationAddress} inputIndex={inputIndex} />
      )}
    </div>
  )
}
```

:::tip
`@cartesi/react` also exports hooks generated for every Cartesi contract, with the ABI and address already set. For example, `useWriteInputBoxAddInput()` returns a `mutate` that only needs `{ args: [applicationAddress, payload] }`, and `useWriteEtherPortalDepositEther()` does the same for Ether deposits.
:::

### 4. Reading Outputs from Cartesi Application

The Cartesi node exposes a JSON-RPC API to fetch the outputs (notices, vouchers and DELEGATECALL vouchers) and reports generated by an application. `useOutputs` and `useReports` return `{ data, pagination }`; each output has a `decodedData` field whose `type` is `Notice`, `Voucher` or `DelegateCallVoucher`. Indexes are `bigint`s and `createdAt` is a `Date`.

A voucher can only be executed after the claim of its epoch is accepted on the base layer. The node returns the output's proof (`outputHashesSiblings`) as soon as it computes the claim, before the claim is accepted, so the component below also checks the epoch's status with `useEpoch` and enables execution only at `CLAIM_ACCEPTED`. `toOutputArgs` turns the output into the arguments of the application contract's `executeOutput` function. Create `src/components/ExecuteVoucher.tsx`:

```tsx title="src/components/ExecuteVoucher.tsx"
import { useEffect } from 'react'
import type { Address } from 'viem'
import { useWaitForTransactionReceipt, useWriteContract } from 'wagmi'
import { useEpoch, useOutput } from '@cartesi/react'
import { toOutputArgs } from '@cartesi/client'
import { iApplicationAbi } from '@cartesi/client/abi'

interface ExecuteVoucherProps {
  applicationAddress: Address
  outputIndex: bigint
}

export function ExecuteVoucher({ applicationAddress, outputIndex }: ExecuteVoucherProps) {
  const { data: output, refetch } = useOutput({
    application: applicationAddress,
    outputIndex,
    refetchInterval: 5000,
  })
  // The node returns the proof as soon as it computes the claim, but the voucher
  // can only be executed once the claim of its epoch has been accepted on chain.
  const { data: epoch } = useEpoch({
    application: applicationAddress,
    epochIndex: output?.epochIndex,
    enabled: output !== undefined,
    refetchInterval: 5000,
  })
  const { mutate: writeContract, data: hash, isPending, error: writeError } = useWriteContract()
  const {
    isLoading: isConfirming,
    isSuccess,
    error: receiptError, // set when the transaction reverts
  } = useWaitForTransactionReceipt({ hash })
  const error = writeError ?? receiptError

  useEffect(() => {
    if (isSuccess) refetch()
  }, [isSuccess, refetch])

  if (!output) return null
  if (output.executionTransactionHash) {
    return <span>Executed in {output.executionTransactionHash.slice(0, 10)}...</span>
  }
  if (isSuccess) return <span>Executed, waiting for the node...</span>
  if (!output.outputHashesSiblings || epoch?.status !== 'CLAIM_ACCEPTED') {
    return <span>Waiting for the epoch's claim to be accepted...</span>
  }

  const execute = () => {
    writeContract({
      address: applicationAddress,
      abi: iApplicationAbi,
      functionName: 'executeOutput',
      args: toOutputArgs(output),
    })
  }

  return (
    <span>
      <button onClick={execute} disabled={isPending || isConfirming}>
        {isPending || isConfirming ? 'Executing...' : 'Execute'}
      </button>
      {error && <span> Failed: {error.message.split('\n')[0]}</span>}
    </span>
  )
}
```

Create `src/components/CartesiOutputs.tsx`. It lists notices, vouchers, DELEGATECALL vouchers and reports, newest first, and refreshes every five seconds:

```tsx title="src/components/CartesiOutputs.tsx"
import { useOutputs, useReports } from '@cartesi/react'
import type { Output, Report } from '@cartesi/client'
import { formatEther, hexToString, type Address } from 'viem'
import { ExecuteVoucher } from './ExecuteVoucher'

interface CartesiOutputsProps {
  applicationAddress: Address
  inputIndex?: bigint
}

interface Row {
  key: string
  type: string
  inputIndex: bigint
  index: bigint
  content: string
  voucherIndex?: bigint
}

const outputRow = (output: Output): Row => {
  const row = { key: `output-${output.index}`, inputIndex: output.inputIndex, index: output.index }
  const decoded = output.decodedData
  switch (decoded?.type) {
    case 'Notice':
      return { ...row, type: 'Notice', content: hexToString(decoded.payload) }
    case 'Voucher':
      return {
        ...row,
        type: 'Voucher',
        content: `To: ${decoded.destination} | Value: ${formatEther(decoded.value)} ETH | Payload: ${decoded.payload}`,
        voucherIndex: output.index,
      }
    case 'DelegateCallVoucher':
      return {
        ...row,
        type: 'Delegate Call Voucher',
        content: `To: ${decoded.destination} | Payload: ${decoded.payload}`,
        voucherIndex: output.index,
      }
    default:
      return { ...row, type: 'Unknown', content: output.rawData }
  }
}

const reportRow = (report: Report): Row => ({
  key: `report-${report.index}`,
  type: 'Report',
  inputIndex: report.inputIndex,
  index: report.index,
  content: `${hexToString(report.rawData)} (${report.createdAt.toLocaleString()})`,
})

export function CartesiOutputs({ applicationAddress, inputIndex }: CartesiOutputsProps) {
  const outputs = useOutputs({
    application: applicationAddress,
    inputIndex,
    descending: true,
    refetchInterval: 5000,
  })
  const reports = useReports({
    application: applicationAddress,
    inputIndex,
    descending: true,
    refetchInterval: 5000,
  })

  if (outputs.isLoading || reports.isLoading) return <div>Loading...</div>
  if (outputs.error) return <div>Error loading outputs: {outputs.error.message}</div>
  if (reports.error) return <div>Error loading reports: {reports.error.message}</div>

  // newest input first, then newest output/report first
  const rows = [
    ...(outputs.data?.data.map(outputRow) ?? []),
    ...(reports.data?.data.map(reportRow) ?? []),
  ].sort((a, b) =>
    a.inputIndex !== b.inputIndex
      ? Number(b.inputIndex - a.inputIndex)
      : Number(b.index - a.index),
  )

  const cell = { padding: '8px', borderBottom: '1px solid #ddd' }

  return (
    <div>
      <h2>Application Outputs</h2>
      <button onClick={() => { outputs.refetch(); reports.refetch() }}>Refresh</button>

      {rows.length === 0 ? (
        <p>No outputs found for this application.</p>
      ) : (
        <table style={{ width: '100%', borderCollapse: 'collapse' }}>
          <thead>
            <tr>
              <th style={cell}>Input Index</th>
              <th style={cell}>Index</th>
              <th style={cell}>Type</th>
              <th style={cell}>Content</th>
              <th style={cell}>Action</th>
            </tr>
          </thead>
          <tbody>
            {rows.map((row) => (
              <tr key={row.key}>
                <td style={cell}>#{row.inputIndex.toString()}</td>
                <td style={cell}>#{row.index.toString()}</td>
                <td style={cell}>{row.type}</td>
                <td style={cell}>
                  <pre style={{ margin: 0, whiteSpace: 'pre-wrap', wordBreak: 'break-all' }}>{row.content}</pre>
                </td>
                <td style={cell}>
                  {row.voucherIndex !== undefined && (
                    <ExecuteVoucher applicationAddress={applicationAddress} outputIndex={row.voucherIndex} />
                  )}
                </td>
              </tr>
            ))}
          </tbody>
        </table>
      )}

      <p>
        Showing {outputs.data?.data.length ?? 0} of {outputs.data?.pagination.totalCount ?? 0} outputs
        and {reports.data?.data.length ?? 0} of {reports.data?.pagination.totalCount ?? 0} reports
      </p>
    </div>
  )
}
```

The `Execute` button uses the connected wallet to send the transaction. A voucher can be executed only once; executing it again reverts.

### 5. Application status

Create `src/components/CartesiStatus.tsx`. It shows the application (`useApplication`), the number of processed inputs (`useProcessedInputCount`), and the latest epochs (`useEpochs`) and inputs (`useInputs`):

```tsx title="src/components/CartesiStatus.tsx"
import { useApplication, useEpochs, useInputs, useProcessedInputCount } from '@cartesi/react'
import type { Address } from 'viem'

interface CartesiStatusProps {
  applicationAddress: Address
}

export function CartesiStatus({ applicationAddress }: CartesiStatusProps) {
  const { data: application, error } = useApplication({ application: applicationAddress })
  const { data: processedInputs } = useProcessedInputCount({
    application: applicationAddress,
    refetchInterval: 5000,
  })
  const { data: epochs } = useEpochs({
    application: applicationAddress,
    descending: true,
    limit: 5,
    refetchInterval: 5000,
  })
  const { data: inputs } = useInputs({
    application: applicationAddress,
    descending: true,
    limit: 5,
    refetchInterval: 5000,
  })

  if (error) return <p>Error loading application: {error.message}</p>
  if (!application) return <p>Loading application...</p>

  return (
    <div>
      <h2>Application {application.name}</h2>
      <p>
        Status: {application.status} | Consensus: {application.consensusType} | Epoch length:{' '}
        {application.epochLength.toString()} blocks | Processed inputs: {processedInputs?.toString()}
      </p>
      <h3>Latest epochs</h3>
      <ul>
        {epochs?.data.map((epoch) => (
          <li key={epoch.index.toString()}>
            Epoch {epoch.index.toString()} (blocks {epoch.firstBlock.toString()}-{epoch.lastBlock.toString()}): {epoch.status}
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
      <h3>Latest inputs</h3>
      <ul>
        {inputs?.data.map((input) => (
          <li key={input.index.toString()}>
            Input #{input.index.toString()} from {input.decodedData?.sender}: {input.status}
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Complete Example

Stitch the components together inside the App. The deposit, inspect and application list components are created in the next sections; create them before running the app.

Replace `src/App.tsx`:

```tsx title="src/App.tsx"
import { useState } from 'react'
import { useConnect, useConnection, useConnectors, useDisconnect } from 'wagmi'
import { getAddress, type Address } from 'viem'
import { CartesiApps } from './components/CartesiApps'
import { CartesiInput } from './components/CartesiInput'
import { CartesiInspect } from './components/CartesiInspect'
import { CartesiOutputs } from './components/CartesiOutputs'
import { CartesiStatus } from './components/CartesiStatus'
import { DepositERC20 } from './components/DepositERC20'
import { DepositEther } from './components/DepositEther'

function App() {
  // checksummed, as the node returns it, so that the selector below matches it
  const [applicationAddress, setApplicationAddress] = useState<Address>(
    getAddress(import.meta.env.VITE_CARTESI_APP_ADDRESS),
  )
  const { isConnected, address } = useConnection()
  const connectors = useConnectors()
  const { mutate: connect } = useConnect()
  const { mutate: disconnect } = useDisconnect()

  return (
    <div>
      <header>
        <h1>Cartesi App Frontend</h1>

        {isConnected ? (
          <div>
            <span>{address?.slice(0, 6)}...{address?.slice(-4)}</span>
            <button onClick={() => disconnect()}>Disconnect</button>
          </div>
        ) : (
          <div>
            {connectors.map((connector) => (
              <button key={connector.uid} onClick={() => connect({ connector })}>
                {connector.name}
              </button>
            ))}
          </div>
        )}
      </header>

      <CartesiApps selected={applicationAddress} onAppSelect={setApplicationAddress} />

      {isConnected ? (
        <main>
          <section>
            <p>App Address: {applicationAddress}</p>
            <CartesiInput applicationAddress={applicationAddress} />
            <DepositEther applicationAddress={applicationAddress} />
            <DepositERC20 applicationAddress={applicationAddress} />
            <CartesiInspect applicationAddress={applicationAddress} />
          </section>
          <section>
            <CartesiStatus applicationAddress={applicationAddress} />
          </section>
          <section>
            <CartesiOutputs applicationAddress={applicationAddress} />
          </section>
        </main>
      ) : (
        <p>Connect your wallet to interact with the Cartesi application.</p>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}

export default App
```

## Bridging of Assets

Assets enter a Cartesi application through the portal contracts, which add an input with the deposit details to the application. The portal ABIs and addresses are exported by `@cartesi/client/abi`: `etherPortalAbi`, `erc20PortalAbi`, `erc721PortalAbi`, `erc1155SinglePortalAbi` and `erc1155BatchPortalAbi`, each with its `...Address`. In rollups-contracts v3 the deposit functions are `depositEther`, `depositErc20Tokens`, `depositErc721Token`, `depositSingleErc1155Token` and `depositBatchErc1155Token`.

### Depositing Ether

Create `src/components/DepositEther.tsx`. It calls `depositEther` on the Ether portal, sending the amount as the transaction value:

```tsx title="src/components/DepositEther.tsx"
import { useState } from 'react'
import { parseEther, stringToHex, type Address } from 'viem'
import { useConnection, useWaitForTransactionReceipt, useWriteContract } from 'wagmi'
import { etherPortalAbi, etherPortalAddress } from '@cartesi/client/abi'

interface DepositEtherProps {
  applicationAddress: Address
}

export function DepositEther({ applicationAddress }: DepositEtherProps) {
  const [amount, setAmount] = useState('')
  const { address } = useConnection()
  const { mutate: writeContract, data: hash, isPending, error } = useWriteContract()
  const { isLoading: isConfirming, isSuccess } = useWaitForTransactionReceipt({ hash })

  const handleDeposit = () => {
    writeContract(
      {
        address: etherPortalAddress,
        abi: etherPortalAbi,
        functionName: 'depositEther',
        args: [applicationAddress, stringToHex(`Deposited ${amount} ether`)],
        value: parseEther(amount),
      },
      { onSuccess: () => setAmount('') },
    )
  }

  const invalid = !amount || Number(amount) <= 0

  return (
    <div>
      <h3>Deposit Ether</h3>
      <label>Amount (ETH): </label>
      <input
        type="number"
        step="0.01"
        placeholder="0.1"
        value={amount}
        onChange={(e) => setAmount(e.target.value)}
        disabled={isPending}
      />
      <button onClick={handleDeposit} disabled={!address || isPending || invalid}>
        {isPending ? 'Depositing...' : 'Deposit'}
      </button>
      {error && <p>Failed to deposit: {error.message.split('\n')[0]}</p>}
      {hash && (
        <p>
          Transaction: <code>{hash}</code> {isConfirming ? '(confirming...)' : isSuccess ? '(confirmed)' : ''}
        </p>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Depositing ERC-20 tokens

An ERC-20 deposit takes two transactions: the owner first approves the ERC-20 portal to move the tokens, then calls `depositErc20Tokens`. The CLI devnet deploys a test token (`testFungibleTokenAddress` in `@cartesi/client/abi`, `TestToken` in `cartesi address-book`) whose `mint` function anyone can call, so the component also offers a mint button for local testing.

Create `src/components/DepositERC20.tsx`:

```tsx title="src/components/DepositERC20.tsx"
import { useState } from 'react'
import { erc20Abi, formatUnits, isAddress, parseUnits, type Address } from 'viem'
import { useConfig, useConnection, useReadContracts, useWriteContract } from 'wagmi'
import { waitForTransactionReceipt } from 'wagmi/actions'
import {
  erc20PortalAbi,
  erc20PortalAddress,
  testFungibleTokenAbi,
  testFungibleTokenAddress,
} from '@cartesi/client/abi'

interface DepositERC20Props {
  applicationAddress: Address
}

export function DepositERC20({ applicationAddress }: DepositERC20Props) {
  const [token, setToken] = useState<string>(testFungibleTokenAddress)
  const [amount, setAmount] = useState('')
  const [status, setStatus] = useState('')
  const config = useConfig()
  const { address } = useConnection()
  const { mutateAsync: writeContractAsync, isPending } = useWriteContract()

  const tokenAddress = isAddress(token) ? token : undefined
  const { data, refetch } = useReadContracts({
    contracts: [
      { address: tokenAddress, abi: erc20Abi, functionName: 'decimals' },
      { address: tokenAddress, abi: erc20Abi, functionName: 'symbol' },
      { address: tokenAddress, abi: erc20Abi, functionName: 'balanceOf', args: [address!] },
    ],
    allowFailure: false,
    query: { enabled: !!tokenAddress && !!address },
  })
  const [decimals, symbol, balance] = data ?? []

  const run = async (label: string, action: () => Promise<void>) => {
    try {
      setStatus(`${label}...`)
      await action()
      setStatus(`${label}: done`)
    } catch (error) {
      setStatus(`${label} failed: ${(error as Error).message.split('\n')[0]}`)
    } finally {
      refetch()
    }
  }

  // devnet only: the CLI's test token lets anyone mint
  const mint = () =>
    run('Mint', async () => {
      const hash = await writeContractAsync({
        address: testFungibleTokenAddress,
        abi: testFungibleTokenAbi,
        functionName: 'mint',
        args: [address!, parseUnits('100', 18)],
      })
      await waitForTransactionReceipt(config, { hash })
    })

  const deposit = () =>
    run('Deposit', async () => {
      if (!tokenAddress || decimals === undefined) throw new Error('invalid token')
      const value = parseUnits(amount, decimals)
      // 1. allow the ERC-20 portal to transfer the tokens
      const approveHash = await writeContractAsync({
        address: tokenAddress,
        abi: erc20Abi,
        functionName: 'approve',
        args: [erc20PortalAddress, value],
      })
      await waitForTransactionReceipt(config, { hash: approveHash })
      // 2. deposit them into the application
      const depositHash = await writeContractAsync({
        address: erc20PortalAddress,
        abi: erc20PortalAbi,
        functionName: 'depositErc20Tokens',
        args: [tokenAddress, applicationAddress, value, '0x'],
      })
      await waitForTransactionReceipt(config, { hash: depositHash })
      setAmount('')
    })

  return (
    <div>
      <h3>Deposit ERC-20</h3>
      <label>Token: </label>
      <input value={token} onChange={(e) => setToken(e.target.value)} size={44} />
      <p>
        Balance: {balance !== undefined && decimals !== undefined ? `${formatUnits(balance, decimals)} ${symbol}` : '-'}
        {token === testFungibleTokenAddress && (
          <button onClick={mint} disabled={!address || isPending}>Mint 100 test tokens</button>
        )}
      </p>
      <label>Amount: </label>
      <input type="number" placeholder="10" value={amount} onChange={(e) => setAmount(e.target.value)} />
      <button onClick={deposit} disabled={!address || isPending || !tokenAddress || !amount}>
        Approve and deposit
      </button>
      {status && <p>{status}</p>}
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Advanced Usage

### Waiting for Input Processing

`InputTracker` above uses `useWaitForInput`. Pass `rejectErrors: true` to make the query fail when the input ends with any status other than `ACCEPTED`, and `pollingInterval`, `retryCount` or `timeout` (milliseconds) to tune the polling. The defaults poll every four seconds, ten times, after which React Query retries the whole wait.

### Inspecting the application state

Inspect requests are plain HTTP calls to the node and have no hook. Create `src/components/CartesiInspect.tsx`:

```tsx title="src/components/CartesiInspect.tsx"
import { useState } from 'react'
import { hexToString, type Address, type Hex } from 'viem'

interface InspectResponse {
  status: string
  reports: { payload: Hex }[]
  processed_input_count: number
  exception_data?: Hex
  error?: string
}

export function CartesiInspect({ applicationAddress }: { applicationAddress: Address }) {
  const [payload, setPayload] = useState('')
  const [result, setResult] = useState<InspectResponse>()
  const [error, setError] = useState('')

  const inspect = async () => {
    setError('')
    try {
      const response = await fetch(`${import.meta.env.VITE_CARTESI_INSPECT_URL}/${applicationAddress}`, {
        method: 'POST',
        body: payload,
      })
      if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`${response.status} ${await response.text()}`)
      setResult(await response.json())
    } catch (e) {
      setError((e as Error).message)
    }
  }

  return (
    <div>
      <h3>Inspect</h3>
      <input value={payload} onChange={(e) => setPayload(e.target.value)} placeholder="Inspect payload" />
      <button onClick={inspect}>Inspect</button>
      {error && <p>Inspect failed: {error}</p>}
      {result && (
        <div>
          <p>Status: {result.status} (processed inputs: {result.processed_input_count})</p>
          <ul>
            {result.reports.map((report, i) => (
              <li key={i}>{hexToString(report.payload)}</li>
            ))}
          </ul>
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Using the Cartesi client directly

Outside React, or for calls without a hook, create the node client with `createCartesiPublicClient` (inside components, `useCartesiClient()` returns the client of the nearest `CartesiProvider`):

```ts
import { http } from 'viem'
import { createCartesiPublicClient } from '@cartesi/client'

const client = createCartesiPublicClient({
  transport: http('http://127.0.0.1:6751/rpc'),
})

const { data: outputs, pagination } = await client.listOutputs({
  application: '0x...',
  limit: 10,
  offset: 0,
})
const nodeInfo = await client.getNodeInfo() // { chainId, version, defaultBlock }
```

### Listing all available applications

Create `src/components/CartesiApps.tsx`:

```tsx title="src/components/CartesiApps.tsx"
import { useApplications } from '@cartesi/react'
import type { Address } from 'viem'

interface CartesiAppsProps {
  selected?: Address
  onAppSelect?: (appAddress: Address) => void
}

export function CartesiApps({ selected, onAppSelect }: CartesiAppsProps) {
  const { data: applications, isLoading, error } = useApplications()

  if (isLoading) return <div>Loading applications...</div>
  if (error) return <div>Error loading applications: {error.message}</div>

  return (
    <div>
      <h2>Cartesi Applications</h2>
      {applications?.data.length === 0 ? (
        <p>No applications found.</p>
      ) : (
        <div>
          <label>Select Application: </label>
          <select value={selected} onChange={(e) => onAppSelect?.(e.target.value as Address)}>
            {applications?.data.map((app) => (
              <option key={app.applicationAddress} value={app.applicationAddress}>
                {app.name} ({app.applicationAddress})
              </option>
            ))}
          </select>
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Run the application

```bash
pnpm dev
```

Open the URL printed by Vite, connect with **Mock Connector** (or **Injected** for MetaMask), and:

1. Send an input and watch `InputTracker` report its status; the notices and reports it produced appear under **Application Outputs**.
2. Deposit Ether or ERC-20 tokens. A deposit is an input sent by the portal, so it also shows up in the inputs and outputs.
3. If your application emits vouchers, wait for the epoch of the voucher to be settled (the epoch status in **Latest epochs** becomes `CLAIM_ACCEPTED`) and click **Execute**.

To type-check and build the application for production:

```bash
pnpm build
```

title: Running applications on a forked network
